Below is a simplified version of my code. It is without the section that adds some mist effects and if night time, adds light effects and with 2 lvl_pc/assets lvls instead of 5 in 3 combinations. It also doesn't have the override that makes my GCW_Campaign day time only.
ModeToLoad and ModeToLoadNight should be defined in each of your modes luas in scriptinit(), and just below that you should have:
SetAssetSet (ModeToLoad, ModeToLoadNight)
ModeToLoad is the part of readdatafile that calls for an mrq file in your wld folder, such as ABC_conquest. ModeToLoadNight is the counterpart MRQ that calls the night.lyr file and should be named something lake ABC_conquest_night.
Code:
Select all
function SetAssetSet (ModeToLoad, ModeToLoadNight)
--Randomly Loads one of the texture sets for the time of day/weather mode
    WeatherMode = math.random(1,3)
    if WeatherMode < 2 then
       ReadDataFile("dc:AssetSets\CommonDayTextures.lvl")
       ReadDataFile("dc:ABC\ABC.lvl", ModeToLoad)
    elseif WeatherMode > 2 then 
	ReadDataFile("dc:AssetSets\CommonNightTextures.lvl")
	ReadDataFile("dc:ABC\ABC.lvl", ModeToLoadNight)
    end

end

posts.author: Caleb1117
posts.content_text:
Just make a msh.option for whatever it is, and add
Code:
Select all
-scale 1.0
if you make it 2.0 it will be twice normal size, 0.5 half size, etc
Then so it will show in ZE at the same size, add to the ODF
Code:
Select all
GeometryScale = "1.0"
and match the size you put in the option.
If you scale objects up too large, sometimes the collision gets glitchy and will = Fail.

posts.content_text: I know I'm criticizing when I REALLY shouldn't be, but I'm an OCD Star Wars nerd, so I can't help it.\nDon't get me wrong the map looks absolutly AMAZING!!!  But, the only inhabitable part of Ryloth is supposedly the constant twilight area (Hence TWI'leks).  The planet rotates on a horizontal axis like Uranus, and on the vertical equator it is always in a state of Twilight.  This is the only habitable part because the planet is so close to the sun that the daytime part is burnt to a crisp and the other side of the planet has never recieved any sunlight, so it is colder than Hoth in the winter.  Fortunately, the twilight area of the equator is the middle of these two extremes and perfectly habitable for the twi'leks. *Starting to ramble, getting to point*\nRyloth's sky, in my opinion should be twilight, not mid-day.  Yes, the OCD kid is focusing on the sky while the rest of the map is absolutley amazing.  You don't have to include this request.  In fact, you might not even see it, idc.  I'm just saying it would be more like Ryloth to be in twilight.

posts.content_text:
Here´s the story of Outer Rim : Unkown Planet and Ryloth : Ambush
-+-+-+-+-+~~~Revans Return~~~+-+-+-+-+-+-
4000 years after the Old Republic era and Revans disappearing in the Outer Rim Regions,his spirit was relived by a group of Cultists, short before Palpatine decided to speak out Order 66. The Cultists formed a grand new army, based on Revans former forces, that menaces the Galaxy.
As the News reach the Republic and the Seperatists, they are both schocked. This new enemy is a danger for the whole Galaxy. Count Dooku and General Grievous are dead, so Nute Gunray sees only one chance of surviving: He associates with the Republic to end their war and fight their new enemy.
Meanwhile in the Senate, Palpatine isn´t happy about this. His plan to destroy the Jedi seems to be broken. He has to wait how the conflict works out.
On an unknown Planet in the Outer Rim Regions, the battle begins...
-+-+-+-+-+~~~Ambush on Ryloth~~~+-+-+-+-+-+-
Revan and some of his Troopers have escaped from their Outer Rim Base shortly before the United Galactic Forces were able to capture the Castle.
Revan and the rest of his army landed on the friendly desert world of Ryloth.
He allied with some strange native Force-sensitive inhabitants there, who had rebuilt the old sith academy there to relive the cult.
The news service of the Republic discovered this new outpost after some weeks. So the United Galactic Forces start the next attack under the command of Anakin Skywalker. His army is trained for jungle environment, but against the advise of Jedimaster Aayla Secura, who stays at the capital ship, he starts the attack without waiting for reinforcements.
The surface of the planet seems to be empty and liveless but Revan has already waited for them ...
Thanks to Bantha55 for helping me

posts.author: Post by Sky_216
posts.content_text:
Hints:
You can stop vehicles getting damaged in water by putting this line in their main ODF:
WaterDamageAmount       = "0.0"
Just make sure you remove the old one.
The "self" pilottype can be really useful. You can do things like add lots more weapons to a vehicle, allow a HMP to fire lots of guided (not homing. guided) missiles at a time, be able to fly a gunship without having to take a bunch of troops away from the battle to fill up the turrets. posts.author: Master Fionwë
posts.content_text:
Finally, I bring to you my first map, improved and expanded. Era said in his review of version 1.0 that it was the biggest map he had ever seen; well, now it is even larger. I have expanded the borders of the map to some of the unused corners. A new mini-map has been put into the map, courtesy of Repsharpshooter. Thanks Rep!
The map has many features in it, some were already in version 1.0, while many are new to this version.
There are an increased number of vehicles now, not quite as many as I had at first, but more than I planned on for this version.
I have added a hidden tunnel to the map, one that is accessed by only one small room using a glitch. There is a nice asset in the tunnel to use if you get there.
I can safely say that this map has been the first to do a few things:
The first to use the SPHA-T as an actual vehicle, the first to use the RTT, and the first to use a hidden model in the geo world folders, called the entryspire. You will see a lot of them scattered around the map.
Bugs still known to exist
:
The LA-AT still does that spinning thing sometimes, but I have seen it fly around like any other flyers.
I think that one of the vehicles is still missing sound.
Effects don't always appear.
A few objects will not stick to the ground. Absolutely nothing could be done about them, so they will be removed in one of the future patches.
There is a lot to be done playing this map. I've tried to make it so that there is a battle going on in many places at once, regardless of what cps you have at any given time. The battle, if left to itself, has a fairly good movie like ending: the Republic wins with heavy losses, after a fierce bloody(and oily) battle, by slowly taking over the field. It is awesome to watch as the clones and Jedi go different ways to get to a cp, and then come out and attack a single cp on multiple sides. If you ever happen to be spawn-camping cp4, watch as Jedi and clones come through the back and side ways.
Of all the cps, only one seems to be messed up. CP11 in the chasm is in the script, but no one goes for it unless they are right there near it, and no one leaves it after it is captured. It does make for a nice struggle as you fight about 50 droids hanging out in it.
Link to the WIP:
W.I.P.
Here are the ss from the wip:
I owe many people for the tools, knowledge, resources, and help for this map. If I forget anyone it is only due to the large number of people that I already mention, and was not intentional.
Credits
;
Thanks especially to the members of Gametoast who helped me out with this map far more than I expected. Teancum, MercuryNoodles, Maveritchell, Trainmaster, and many others, for the help they gave me with this map's many issues during the stages of it's progress.
Thanks guys, this map wouldn't have even come out without your help.
Teancum for the source files, Luminara, Shaakti, Plokoon, and some vehicles, dwarfspider and geofighter, for releasing them; and the creators of these.
Psych0Fred for some of the vehicles; sphat, command shuttle,
AceMastermind for the core ship model I used
OOM-9, I hope I got the name right, the creator of the DC-15 model
The creator of the DH-17 model
Delta_57_Dash for the Disruptor Rifle
Vyse for the vibroblade
Moving Target and Murdocr for the ARC Rifle model
Challenger33 for the hex-edited jettrooper model and for some good ideas for the map
AlexSecura for the support he's given me and some good ideas
Repsharpshooter for the mini-map and also for some good ideas
Yankfan for the cool lasers,
Both YankFan and a_speck_of_dust for the CIS side, and the fixed dwarf spider that came with it.
[RDH]Zerted for the awesome help with scripts, especially ctf. Sadly, CTF did not work out very well, possibly because of the map's size, but thanks man anyways! It was looking great when it did work!
Beta testers

Repsharpshooter

REivEN

YankFan
CaptainOrdo11
My brother for getting the game in the first place
Lucasarts for creating such a great game, and
George Lucas for creating such an awesome galaxy.
Battle of Geonosis; 125th Legion
Unfortunately, due to the amount of homework that I ended up having, the map is not as finished as I wanted it to be, and there might be a few glitches that I missed due to time rush. For the most part it is finished though. As you will see, there are 3 modes, Conquest, Hunt, and Assault. Assault is my attempt at creating an online stable mode, and Hunt is only there for future purposes. I need to rewrite the script for it.
I am a little disappointed by the outcome of the map, but I wanted to get it out before I leave for the next two weeks to Europe.
Oh, the readme is screwed up, since notepad has (very oddly) become very messed up recently on my computer. It adds this \par at the end of every line now. Nothing works, since even getting rid of them and saving it will reinsert them again. Sorry for the inconveniance of having to read that.
I am done with the main file for this map, although I will continue to work on it and improve upon what I have, polishing it up and dealing with any glitches found slowly. I'll upload patches, containing only the fixed files for the map, as I complete them.
IMPORTANT: Do not play either Hunt yet, as neither of them work properly. One crashes and the other lost the command posts. They are in progress right now, to be released after I return in early June.

posts.author: Post by Eggman
posts.content_text:
Aldura Series Release Thread
Beachhead Beta:
Hidden/Spoiler:
Map Details:
In addition to being a beta for the map itself, this release is also serving as a preview for the Aldura Campaign map series as a whole, although it won't actually end up being the first map in the story (if that's confusing, read through the WIP topic for further explanation).
Modes:
CW Conquest
CW Campaign
Screens:
Credits:
Pahricida - DC-15A model
AceMastermind - help with Pahricida's model, OOM-9 and security droid models
EGG_GUTS - OOM-9 texture
OOM-9 - DC-15S model
Teancum - any Conversion Pack assets
Dragonum/Jawa_Killer - any ML Kashyyyk assets
Dann Boeing - ODF guide
Snork - Base readme template
RC-1290 - Mission Scripting tutorial
If anybody is missing from the credits, please notify me immediately so I can make the correction.
Aldura #1: Orbital Assault
Hidden/Spoiler:
Story:
The CIS has taken control of the planet Aldura. Although Aldura's industrial contribution to the war is minimal, the planet's position in the galaxy provides a strong tactical advantage to the faction controlling it. Knowing this, the Republic has sent a large invasion force to break the CIS blockade and liberate the planet....
Modes:
CW Campaign - only mode for now; I have some others planned that will be included in a future update
Screens:
Credits:
AceMastermind - Droid control ship w/ hangars
Teancum - Conversion pack assets (V-19s)
Dragonum/Jawa_Killer - Laser textures from ML Kashyyyk assets, CIS frigate models
Wazmol - Acclamator models
Included in this download are the map, the Readme, and a walkthrough for the objectives in case anybody gets confused, since I'm leaving in two days and won't be back to answer questions until the end of July.
Aldura #2: Landfall
Hidden/Spoiler:
Story:
Republic forces have pushed through the Separatist
blockade over Aldura and landed on the surface. The
primary objective for the first wave is to take control of
the capital city of the continent of Serena. As thousands
of Republic soldiers descend on the city, the CIS
scrambles to establish a defense....
Modes:
CW Campaign - follow the story of CT - 9/5262, a rookie clone trooper being deployed in his first battle
CW Conquest - typical conquest gameplay; play as either Republic or CIS and fight for control of four command posts along the length of the street
Screens:
Credits:
Dragonum/Jawa_Killer - One or two effects from the ML Kashyyyk assets
OOM-9 - DC-15S model
Pahricida - DC-15A model
AceMastermind - OOM-9 and security droid models
EGG_GUTS - OOM-9 texture
Syth - DC-15 Marine Rifle model, back-pack addon, thermal detonator model
Squipple/Eddie - models from "SqueddiesSourceModels" pack
DarthD.U.C.K. - DC-17 Hand Blaster model
Hebes24 - throwable orbital strike beacon .odfs used as reference for creating my own orbital strike weapon
Members and staff at Gametoast.com - endless help and support
Download links:
Beachhead Beta:
http://files.filefront.com/AL1exe/;1017 ... einfo.html
Orbital Assault:
http://files.filefront.com/ALSexe/;1071 ... einfo.html
Landfall:
http://files.filefront.com/Aldura+Landf ... einfo.html
If anybody is missing from the credits for either map, please notify me immediately so I can make the correction.
For further details regarding these maps and others coming in the future, please view the WIP thread:
http://www.gametoast.com/forums/viewtop ... 29&t=13557
Thank you for downloading, and please post any comments, questions, or suggestions here.

It is a pity you can't finish this map. I hope you will change your mind and stay in modding Battlefront II, finish all the projects you started, and then quit. You don't have to, it's just my opinion. Anyways, keep up the good work!

posts.author: Post by Maveritchell
posts.content_text:
I only played through the Talay map; I was checking out campaign. You did a fantastic job on the map itself, I thought you used the assets really well to create the feel you were looking for (I haven't played any of the Dark Forces series, so I can't really comment on accuracy, though).
Couple suggestions, though - and maybe they're just food for thought if you're not really planning on changing anything.
1) Minimap. Please. On any campaign/exploratory map this is very necessary. It's tough enough trying to figure out where to go when you're not really given a whole lot of hints - without a minimap it can get to be drudgery. By the same token, you could have used objective markers or even on-map hints (i.e. an indication of where water is on the map).
2) Length. Although it can take a long time to do a single objective, that's only going to be on the first playthrough. Once you've played through it once, there's not much incentive to play again with only three objectives.
3) Sound, sound, beautiful sound. You could have made that map fantastic by adding some rainfall soundregions and maybe even some background music.
4) And this is just a personal preference - add some stuff in there to really spook out the player, like some patrolling AT-STs. Something the player would have to think twice about before taking on with a pistol.
All in all, I really like campaign modes of any kind, this one was definitely fun, albeit short.

Culvar wrote:
What about ARC Captain Alpha-77, Fordo? He'd be a great Republic gunner IMO. Nice models BTW.
We work with a 'semi-hero' system. Mappers like for example FOOLIS make a hero just a unit with points to unlock, since that would be more logical (with hero being the highest class; a normal hero can be quickly available) We use 2 heroes per map, one hero just set up like the normal heroes: these are mostly the key figure (probably jedi, or durge) from the map, and a semi-hero fullfilled by 18 points to unlock. Those are for examples Commander Fordo, Bacara, but even other heroes.. It just all depends on the map. And some maps have one hero, like Jabiim: Shelter Base. It was not real canon to have more as Grievous vs Mace Windu there..
Hope this answers your question

title: How to:Install BETA 1.3 and keep 1.2 patch installed.
author: Ace_Azzameen_5

posts.author: Ace_Azzameen_5
posts.content_text:
It's Simple!
1.Open  C:\program files\lucasarts\star wars battlefront\gamedata*
2.Right Click on 'Battlefront.exe' and then click rename. Type in a name of your choice. 'Battlefront1.2' is my suggestion.
3.Download and install patch 1.3
4.Right click the renamed battlefront.exe and create a shortcut to place on your desktop.
5.To start version 1.3, start swbf normally. To play v1.2, use the new shortcut.
*If installed SWBF in a different place, you probably know what to do . . .

posts.author: Post by Eggman
posts.content_text:
Alright, here's the current layout for sides:
Republic: All clones are Phase I. The side is organized by a combination of rank and classes. Each rank has proper colors on its armor.
Clone trooper:
DC-15A rifle
DC-17 pistol
Thermal detonators x4
Clone Sergeant:
DC-15S carbine
DC-17 pistol
Thermal detonators x4 (this'll probably change so it's not so much like the normal trooper)
Clone Lieutenant:
Rocket Launcher
DC-17 pistol
Thermal detonators x2
Mines x3
Clone Captain:
DC-15x sniper rifle
DC-17 pistol
Undecided on secondary weapons
Clone Engineer:
DC-17 pistol
Fusion cutter
Detpacks x3
Ammo/Health dispenser
Clone Commander:
DC-15A rifle
DC-17 pistol
Electrobinoculars (with orbital strike)
Thermal detonators x4
CIS: Right now, my plan is for each class to only be assigned the one weapon essential to its class. This actually works out pretty well balance wise in this map, and in the second map the CIS actually had a huge advantage before I adjusted a few things in the Republic's favor.
B1 Battledroid:
E-5 blaster rifle
B1 Assault droid:
Rocket launcher
B1 Assassin droid:
E-5s sniper rifle
B1 Engineer droid:
Fusion cutter (to make the engineer a little more useful, the fusion cutter can now heal your allies and yourself)
B2 Super battledroid: Slower, but more durable than shipped version
Wrist blaster (more powerful)
I may add in a command droid with the same orbital strike capabilities as the clone commander.
Grev wrote:
You may want to change the sky to be more... War torn. Unless you are looking for a happy environment!
I'm not completely set on the sky yet, but a theme I'm going for in the atmosphere of these maps is contrast. For example, the second map is set on a grassy, peaceful plains area with a beautiful sunset, but there are burnt out wrecks of vehicles and corpses lying around from a previous battle. Anyway, I might play around with the sky some more to see if I can find something better.

Well, since the first post still hasn't shown up, I'm going to go ahead and re-post the story and description of the project, just so anyone seeing the thread for the first time can actually have some clue as to what's going on. Whenever the original post shows back up, I can just delete this one.
Story: Several months after the outbreak of the Clone Wars, the CIS invaded the world of Aldura. Although Aldura's industrial impact on the war is small, the planet's position in the galaxy gives a significant tactical advantage to the faction controlling it. The Repbulic immediately sent a fleet of ships carrying legions of soldiers to retake the world. The battle for Aldura degenerated into a bitter stalemate, with each side controlling one of the two main continents on the planet. Now the Republic makes one last desperate attempt to drive the CIS off of the world.
Map Description: This the first map of what will be a series of several. In this map, the Republic assaults a small coastal town occupied by the CIS in order to create a beachhead for the coming campaign. The town has been shattered by a previous orbital bombardment.
If you haven't gathered it from previous posts, one of my lofty goals for this series to take a stab at campaign mode.

It'll be the first map I release. I've gone through loads of half-finished maps trying to figure out how everything works. The idea for this particular series has been kicking around in my head for a really long time, though, and has gone through a lot of changes. Originally it was going to take place during the time of Phase II clones and start off with a space map as the Republic tried to break through the blockade of the planet (after I finish the main maps of the series I'm thinking of making some spin-off maps, so I might revive this map and just make it with ships and units from earlier in the war). I got about 50% done with that map over the summer, then the .wld file got corrupted somehow and I couldn't fix it. After that, I put the idea on the shelf for a while, then a few months later I got the itch to start it again. I started with this map originally using the Naboo assets, but I decided I didn't like it, so I scrapped it. At that point I got a little frustrated and decided to give up on making a series. One idea for a map though, the one that'll be the next map in this series, I was still attached to, so I started work on it to just be an independent map. I got around 75% done with that one, and decided to take another stab at making this map. This time I used the Rhen Var assets, and I just dived right into it, and it's turned out better than I would have expected. So yeah, that's my long-winded explanation of the history of this series.
Edit: I have the flyers following paths now without crashing. Aldura: Landfall
After being away for a good five weeks, I've finally been able to get some work done on the next map.
Story:
Republic forces have broken the CIS blockade and landed on Aldura's surface. The first wave must secure a landing zone before moving toward the main concentration of droid forces on the continent. The designated landing zone is a rural farm due to the large, open fields. Although the farm was seized by the CIS early in the occupation of the planet, its only use was as an outpost for scouting patrols, so defenses should be light.
Map Description:
Throughout the course of the battle, you will move through three different areas: a farm, a forest, and a meadow. The farm consists of two fairly large fields and several buildings. The fields have become overgrown with grass and brush due to several months of neglect. Next, you travel through a long and twisting forest path (perfect for ambushes
). Last, you arrive at a peaceful-looking meadow for the final stage of the battle.

I said earlier that I would work on game modes next, but after working on conquest a bit I decided that I wanted to rebuild the sides from the ground up in order to ensure that there wasn't any extra clutter in their folders and because there were some other things I wanted to fix up or change. posts.content_text:
Update time (finally
)!
The mountain rendition of the Landfall map wasn't working out so well either, so the map has been redesigned for the third, and I assure you, last, time. I bring you:
Aldura: Landfall (version 3)
This map was actually already in planning stages, but I decided to move the landfall mission up to this map for a variety of reasons. I was having trouble perfecting the environments of the previous maps, and they were just boring. The mission now takes place in the streets of a modern spaceport city and the objectives are much different, making for a more exciting map.
Mission: The first wave of Republic landing forces caught the CIS off-guard and was able to capture several landing zones in the capital city of Alda, one of two main continents on the planet. However, the CIS responded quickly and established a strong defense in the streets. Your mission is to destroy the artillery cannons at the end of a major roadway that are preventing the Republic's heavy vehicles from moving into the heart of the city. If the CIS is ousted from the city, it will lose its hold on the entire continent and be forced to retreat.
Modes: As usual, campaign and conquest modes are in the works right now. A rough draft for campaign mode is finished, so I'll be going through it and adding all the fine details over the next few weeks. After that, I'll work on conquest mode, which shouldn't take too long, and time permitting, I may consider a CTF mode.
Sides: Same as before, but the CIS now has droidekas, at least for one of the campaign objectives.
Screenshots:

As always, progress will be pretty haphazard, but feedback is appreciated.

Aldura: Doom
Story:
Several months after the initial landings of Republic troops, the planet is still locked in brutal warfare. Although the continent of Serena was seized from the CIS according to plan, the invasion of the other main continent has been unsuccessful. The first waves of ground troops were delayed in orbit, granting the Separatists sufficient time to establish a seemingly impenetrable defense of their major strongholds. Republic forces were routinely decimated in battles against the massive droid armies. Soon the Republic's holdings were limited to only scattered small towns. Now one of those towns has been attacked, and the surviving clone troopers flee across the desolated landscape in an attempt to escape the pursuing droids....
Game modes:
Campaign
Conquest
Uber/XL
Screenshots:

--Update--
Aldura: Ambush
(formerly Aldura: Doom)
-Revised info-
Story:
Several months after the initial landings of Republic troops, the planet is still locked in brutal warfare. Although the continent of Serena was seized from the CIS according to plan, the invasion of the other main continent, Alda, has been unsuccessful. The first waves of ground troops were delayed in orbit, granting the Separatists sufficient time to establish a seemingly impenetrable defense of their major strongholds. The battle for Alda quickly degenerated into a bitter stalemate with staggering losses on both sides. Now the CIS has launched an effort to force the Republic off the continent. After a surprise attack on a Republic base, surviving clone troopers flee across the desolated landscape....
Game Modes:
-Campaign
-Conquest

posts.author: Jediguy
posts.content_text:
Sad to see that this is your last map, but then I noticed Felucia. Junia was a great map and so is this one.
+
Excellent combat (and you're never far from it), with a nice mix of vehicles and infantry. The skins were awesome, especially the clones. I also thought that the addition of N-1s and UT-ATs in CW mode was great. Well-laid out map with near-perfect item, building, and CP placemnet. The sides are evenly balanced and each unit has the right amount of health and ammo. The sides and gameplay in GCW mode were also good. Reinforcement count really makes it feel like a big battle.
-
Fortunately, there is little to say in the con category.  The SBD was a little messed up, at least on my PC. Also, the UT-AT was a little too weak.There is also a small thing that bothered me with Captain Fordo, in that he only had 2 weapons, and they weren't that great. I also wish that the Clone assasin could block blasterfire. also, a lot of things aren't localized in GCW mode.
Overall this was a very fun map to play, especially in the Clone Wars.The highlight was flying over the 2 main droid CPs, strafing and "bombing" the tinnies into scrap metal. Oh, and bonus points for including Darman, but a few points taken off for not including Fi.
:clone:  Overall 9.4/10

posts.author: Skipper 24
posts.content_text:
Ok here is how to install BFX 2.1 while retaining full functionality of the 2.0 Convo pack.
1. Install BFII
2. Official 1.1 patch
3. BFX 2.1
4. Cut the BFX folder from your addon to your desktop. There should now be no BFX folder in your addon.
5. install the convo pack.
6. Cut the BFX folder from your desktop back into your addon.
7. Play BFII. Everything is still there even the KoTOR era which will dissapear unless you follow my instructions.
If you don't have complete functionality re install BFII after step4.

posts.author: Post by Maveritchell
posts.content_text:
Fear is sort've the opposite of Force Valor - Force Valor buffs you and nearby friendlies (a little in both attack and defense). Fear debuffs nearby enemies in both attack and defense.
There are actually a lot of KotOR-era Jedi/Sith with buffing abilities - using them well (Battle Meditation + Force Storm/Wave is
devastating
) is the key to making the Jedi that have them powerful. (Fear plus a well-timed saber throw can kill a Jedi in one hit there and back.)
I know you spent a lot of time on this, but his anims just looked way cooler, and more, uh, how to put it... Professional in the sides beta. But I like the new gun model, kudos to Rep (he made it, right?)
Haha, that was actually something I forgot to change back, I was playing around with mixing Calo's anims with the dual pistol anims I originally made. The plus side with these is that now his guns actually point forward instead of towards the center.

posts.author: Post by Gogie
posts.content_text:
Quick tutorial to save the day!
first off create 4 different layers open up the layer editor by pressing the 6 key. name them ###_bones, ###_rig, ###_mesh, ###_shadow volume... like so.
no layer should be visible or selectable except your bones layer...
next close off your layer window and open up an explorer window (8 key), after that is open press the "L" key to arrange your objects and bones into the layer. arrange them like so...
after all that is done, select the bones you wish to use for this animations and hit the C key to rotate them to where you want them to be in this animation, when it is done rotated to your satisfactory, hit the image of the key at the bottom of your screen (it should be either yellow or green) remember, every part of an attack can not be over 10 frames long (except the final attack which can be 20 frames), dont forget to put a key frame at frames 0, 1 and 10, and don't forget to hide frame 0 (since its your basepose) and start your animation at frame 0. you should ocassionally make sure none of your mesh colides with anoter part of it, check this by unhiding the mesh layer and playing your animations.
when your animations is complete prepare to export, i find it easier to overwrite an existing player animations and then just rename it after the animation munge. (branch select the DummyRoot and make sure your mesh layer is hidden)
when you export your screen should look like this. (for this example im rewriting the dooku animations)
now munge your animation by going to C:\BF2_ModTools\data_###\Animations\SoldierAnimationBank\dooku and clicking on munge.bat....
after that go to C:\BF2_ModTools\data_###\Sides\CIS\MUNGED and rename dooku.zafbin, dooku.zafbin and dooku.anims to [youranimation].zaabin etc.
rewrite yoyur characters odf file to say
AnimationName 		= "[youranimation]"
munge your world and your done.
[edit: set your frame selection to fram 1 before exportation]

posts.author: Post by AceMastermind
posts.content_text:
You don't need layers.
If you're using unit_template_beta you don't need to export a basepose either since these are already in the assets, just animate the bones and export the animation.
If you animate using IK, expressions or constraints then you'll need to plot the animation to the bones before exporting, bones need keys to work in SWBF2, keys on bone chain roots and effectors are no good.
Press F1 and have a look through the XSI docs for more information about animating and also look through the
animation_guide.doc
for guidelines to follow.
Edit: yukisuna changed her question about layers while posting my reply

posts.author: Taivyx
posts.content_text:
Hm, are you guys sure about that Cobalt Force advantage?
Because I just played through it as Marines, and won by a margin of around 100 reinforcements.
Perhaps it's easier to use a run and gun strategy using Cobalt Force since the AK47 has a two shot kill, and the Mac10 has such low spread.
As a Marine you've gotta take cover, stay in cover, and use the strategy defined in the readme.
You'll get numerous kills if you use that strategy with any side, actually.
And keep in mind that the AI use a run and gun strategy unfortunately, so I suppose I can see where that cobalt force advantage comes into play.
Did I mention that various body positions are more accurate than others, and that a two to four shot burst firing pattern is recommended?

posts.content_text:
tsurugi13 wrote:
I liked the way the snipers were balanced, but the scope textures seemed too tall for their width.
That's because I have a widescreen monitor, so while it's in the shape of a circle on my monitor, it would be an oval on standard ratio monitors.

I wouldn't say no to an assault rifle (maybe the first class on either team?) with burst fire.
Well, one of earliest versions of this sides test did have the M16, which had semi-auto and burst fire options.
But, after some heavy testing, I decided to go in favor of a fully automatic rifle, so I scrapped the M16 and released it.

posts.author: Post by jedimaster745
posts.content_text:
Island is my latest map. its a somewhat simple map, built to be simple with simple game modes and simple gameplay. At least that is my sense of the map. But simple can be good, right? Anyways, this is what i've been working on recently. i was kind of bored so i started this as a little fun project. Island was not meant to be a seriously awesome map, and neither was it intended to be better than my previous map: Lost Valley. But it was intended to be utterly; stunningly visually beautiful. Personally i dislike the word beautiful, but that is the one word i would pick to describe this map. I hope you, the downloaders, think this map is beautiful too.
There are two game modes: GCW conquest and CW conquest. CW conquest is a simple campaign mode where the objectives are to locate some crashed ship called the Destroyer II while fending off against gamorrean inhabitants. Its not a hard mission and the objectives are relatively simple. theres a flash speeder just in case the player finds the mission too hard and needs some extra fire power.
GCW conquest is just regular conquest, but the rebels have been replaced with naboo guards who have been renamed the Royal Guards. The Royal Guards of what? I'm not entirely sure, but at least it's better than Naboo Guards. Some of the 'Royal Guards' have different weapons than normal. This was done to help balance the gameplay.
Screenshots at:
http://www.xfire.com/screenshots/jedima
... c3444b.png
I recommend turning your settings to the highest quality possible as it adds to the visual appeal. except for light bloom, that doesnt help at all(at least for me it doesnt).
Credits:
Flashspeeder -Pandemic? correct me if i'm wrong, please.
**THIS MAP MAY NOT BE REDISTRIBUTED BY ANYONE EXCEPT ME, GAME_JEDI/JEDIMASTER745**
Download:
http://files.filefront.com/ISLzip/;1339 ... einfo.html
Please leave comments!

posts.author: Commander_Keller
posts.content_text:
hi all!
inspired by the clone wars series i made a mygeeto remake, clone wars style. originally i just wanted to do this for my own because mygeeto seems to be my favorite map.
this is my first side mod ever and i have to say it turned out to be real fun so i decided to release it. gameplay is good balanced even with all those changes i did to the sides:
Hidden/Spoiler:
the heavy trooper is now a demo specialist and carries a dc-15e (=dc-15a with underbarrel grenade launcher) and demo charges. he has no rocket launcher and he has standard health and standard speed.
the engineer has been changed to a heavy weapons specialist who is armed with that underhand minigun. as he carries a very heavy weapon he is slower.
the sniper is a scout now. i tried to imitate the scouts seen in the clone wars movie by reskinning dragonum's commander cody.
the jet trooper's emp launcher model has been changes into that of a t-21 which i don't know who i have to credit for.
captain rex has an authentic, correct skin and he carries an improved dc-15a with a higher firing rate. he also fields an eweb gun. there is only one captain rex. note: the eweb falls through the ground when setting it on the streets. that is related to the mygeeto map itself. this issue turned out to be good for tactical balancing since you cannot place the eweb in the middle of the street and slaughter droids. you can place the eweb on platforms for example (you will find out).
i added a blizzard commando unit to the rep side. he carries a dlt-19 with an underbarrel grenade launcher  as first weapon.
the rep hero is anakin. the deflecting has been changed similar to that known from bfx which makes more sense and is even more fair and fun to play.
the super battle droid is now really a super battle droid. one could compare them to a moving tank. he moves slower but has 800 health. the wrist blasters have now muzzle flashes.
the officer has been changed to a magna guard with an electro staff. his health is also 800 since i couldn't figure out how to get the deflecting working without crashing the game when playing as cis or rep hero.
speaking of which, the cis hero is count dooku's assassin asajj ventress. her defleting is the same as anakin's.
i added a commando droid to the cis side which carries a modified rifle (same values as the blizzard's weapon) and a bulldog.
on the rep side i have put at-rt's in there instead of hover tanks.
the aat skin and the at-rt skins have been changed and the at-rt's secondary weapon is the same as a hover tank's with different trail effects.
some weapons have modified scopes (scope textures) which look better.
some units have been given backpacks.
bolts/lasers have been changed in color, also the minigun's bolts are now blue which you can actually see.
the sky has been changed to that of a dusk-like sky.
there is so much i am pretty sure that i forgot something. but a pictures tells more than 1000 words so let's cut that verbal diarrhea...
screenshots:
http://img220.imageshack.us/img220/6386/aat.jpg
http://img17.imageshack.us/img17/2005/commandodroid.jpg
http://img10.imageshack.us/img10/5536/1 ... andaat.jpg
http://img160.imageshack.us/img160/5454 ... atatrt.jpg
http://img214.imageshack.us/img214/2375/blizzard.jpg
http://img213.imageshack.us/img213/9029 ... atdemo.jpg
http://img90.imageshack.us/img90/5664/s ... rooper.jpg
http://img24.imageshack.us/img24/1487/rex2y.jpg
http://img17.imageshack.us/img17/9577/rex1.jpg
http://img26.imageshack.us/img26/6637/h ... eeling.jpg
http://img10.imageshack.us/img10/306/engineerfiring.jpg
note: this is not a mod for children. don't expect any super weapon, every unit has its strength. the dtl-19 for example has a slightly lower firing rate but packs a good puch. you cannot stupidly run and cut through enemy units or celebrate a spray and pray "tactic". that would only cost you ammo.
all the skins i used and a couple of bonus skins you can get here:
http://www.gametoast.com/forums/viewtop ... 64&t=17693
i hope you enjoy that mygeeto remake. thanks to gametoast and all the toasters.
have a good time!
keller

posts.author: jedimoose32
posts.content_text:
IRIDONIA: DOCKING STATION
by Jedimoose32
-------------------------
INTRODUCTION
In the midst of the Yuuzhan Vong war, Shedao Shai sent out a company of his finest warriors
to the planet Iridonia in order to determine whether it would make a good terraform world.  The
warriors found the system to be heavily guarded by a fleet of New Republic capital ships.  In the
ensuing space battle, most of the Vong were killed, and the only warriors that reached the planet
either stowed aboard in the ammo containers of 3 K-Wing gunships or managed to fake capture on a
small New Republic prisoner vessel.  The crew of the prison ship was soon killed, but crashed in
a scrapyard conjoined to an Iridonian spaceport, leaving only about 250 survivors of the original
400 that boarded the ship.  A single Mon Calamari capital ship pursued the prison ship and docked
in the nearest terminal.  By chance, the K-Wing escort assigned to the capital ship was none other
than the 3 unsuspecting carriers of nearly 50 Vong warriors, who discreetly disembarked as each
K-Wing landed, refueled, and left.  Meanwhile, the New Republic had the Iridonian Security Guards
evacuate the spaceport of all civilians and non-combat personnel, and then take up strategic
positions all around the docking station.  They had no idea what they were to be dealing with...
After nearly a whole year, Iridonia: Docking Station has been updated.  Although I had originally
planned to only make a small update to Version 1.1, the list of necessary alterations has grown
to the point where I have to call it an overhaul.  This is Iridonia: Docking Station, Version 2.0!
Since April 2008, data has been collected, knowledge has been gained, software has been purchased,
and opinions have been analyzed.  Finally, this March 25th, I began the process of compiling all
that I had gathered into my map.  I hope everyone who plays Version 2.0 enjoys it 2.0 times as
much as they liked 1.0!
CHANGES
-added local Security Guard team
-remodeled Vong amphistaff
-created couffee knife model
-tweaked Vong and Jedi properties
-removed awful K-Wing Hovercrafts
-authenticated ShaperTools model
-enclosed some areas of the map
-added more props for beauty and strategic importance
-replaced barriers to achieve better AI navigation (this was painful, replaced approx. 130 barriers
and added approx. 110 new ones)
-placed dozens more hint nodes, putting the "I" into AI
-Photoshopped the sky (changed to higher resolution, balanced colors, brightened, sharpened, etc.)
-added Health and Ammo droids to all CP's
-fixed spawn paths
|----------------------------------------|
|-------------<INSTALLATION>-------------|
|----------------------------------------|
1. Download Iridonia: Docking Station v2.0.
2. UnRAR the file.
3. Move the folder named "IRI" into the
following directory:
"C:\Program Files\LucasArts\Star
Wars Battlefront II\GameData\addon".
4. If you don't have the addon folder
already, create it in the GameData folder.
5. Run Battlefront II and enjoy!
|----------------------------------------|
KNOWN BUGS/ISSUES
-Shedao Shai and Tionne still lock their upper-body animations for a few seconds every time after
using their power
-name for the Security team members always shows up as [NULL] if you kill them
CREDITS AND THANKS
JediGuy - Feedback, ideas, etc.
AlexSecura - Re-uploading v1.0 when it disappeared
JPIDictatorforlife - Constructive Criticism
Teancum - "Everything You Need v2.0" (total life-saver)
Everyone else at Gametoast:  Although names might escape me, I want to recognize everyone who posted
on the original release topic for Iridonia: Docking Station.  It was on those comments that the idea

posts.author: RogueKnight
posts.content_text:
Well, it appears this has been bumped up, so I might as well add useful information.
I had a conversation with Rep on Xfire, and I worked out how to add hardpoints in sketchup.
Hardpoints don't have to be nulls, they can just be a regular mesh.
Bear with me, as I may miss a few things, and this is going to apply to a gun.
1)Take your gun model, and put a 3D cube where you want the hp_fire to be.
2)Select the cube, go to Edit>18 Entities>Make Group
3)Right-click on your new group, and click Entity Info
4)Change the name to hp_fire, and check the hidden box.
5)Click the X to close the window
6)Repeat for the hp_active
7)Export to a .kmz, the extract the kmz and open the collada file in a collada-compatible program such as milkshape/XSI/Autodesk/Blender ect......
8 )Check to make sure your meshes still register with their names, then follow the tutorial to make it battlefront compatible.
EDIT: I just got the Sketchup SDK, and I'm going to try to write a plugin that automatically changes inverted polies to normals when exporting to .kmz. I may also try to work out a grid so that models can be scaled down properly.
EDIT2: What I'm trying to do may not be possible, so I may just try to find a way to only work in normals. On a second note, there is some pretty key sketchup info here, so in the event that this is locked, shall I make a new topic with all the data from this thread?

posts.author: Post by minilogoguy18
posts.content_text: Hard points and envelope deformers don't have to be nulls and 2d/3d chains, they can be geometry. Hell, I'm pretty sure you can just script in the .odf file to use the actual model as a hard point and just change it's offset so that every effect doesn't come from the center of the model. All of the hierarchy nodes can be geometry as well, pandemic had all the hardpoints and the dummyroots of their models as geometry. And since I've animated hardpoints that were geometry to move to follow bones like on the B-Wing, it should be possible to just use geometry for bones. These are all things to consider so that XSI wont be needed as much and you could move things straight from sketchup.\nBut there could be a problem, if sketchup is unable to create envelopes, arrange a hierarchy or animate then the program is useless since you could just use mod tool and convert it through a few programs. Some of these may only really be possible if the program is actually still being developed to have more features but since it's free it's unlikely, everyone has to make a livin'.

There's no error, it's just that hero assault requires more resources than normal and that will make it tricky to host if you don't have a lot of bandwidth.
Dom380 wrote:
you play as starkiller but you fight an evil version of yourself in the last wave (and its very very hard)
You actually fight the opposite of whatever you played as. Coruscant wave mode you can either play light-side or dark-side. If you play lightside, you fight Sith and eventually yourself. If you play darkside, you fight Jedi and eventually yourself.
Some clues for the seventh wave modes:
Coruscant: Kill X before the wave ends
Death Star: Kill 14 X
Felucia: Kill both X
Kashyyyk: Kill 3 X and maintain 10+ X

posts.author: Xavious
posts.content_text:
Hey all, if you frequent the Glamour Shots topic you may have already seen some early pics of this mod. I'm now at the point where I can announce and show off my most recent work.
I'm taking a forced break from mapping for the time being, seeing as my ZeroEditor is having serious crashing problems. If you remember my Gylesh: Seabed WIP, then you know what I'm talking about. Basically, I don't want to risk corrupting my maps due to these crashes. However, I found that I still had an undying desire to mod, despite the fact that I couldn't map. Thus, this project was born. Once I've solved my ZE problems, I'll continue Gylesh, but for now, this mod is my focus.
This is an era mod which adds the Ultimate Clone Wars era to all shipped maps. The UCW era consists of a new unit set-up which is essentially a much-improved version of the idea behind the KotOR sides I used in my Earth: Town map. Also, while this mod may contain some canon parts, there's also some non-canon things, such as my 607th legion and some other made-up units. Some notable features include:
-Random clone legions, commando units, and heroes for all maps. (Thanks to Mav's random heroes script)
-AI Heroes
-Enhanced side layout
-New lasers, sounds, effects, etc.
-New characters based on the Clone Wars television series
-Balance and difficulty similar to the shipped game. (Maybe a little bit harder)
-New maps (once I get ZE working) For now, I've got a couple of mostly finished maps I'll be using, such as Torvik: Sunken City and Dantooine: Lakeside.
-
Maybe
some new gamemodes. (Siege/ Prison Break)
-Possible edited melee combat system
Sides:
The sides consist of three basic classes: a light unit, a medium unit, and a heavy unit. Unlockable classes include a support unit, a melee unit, and a commado. Other classes vary by legion, and include units such as commanders or unique, non-Hero units.
Medium Class (Clone Trooper/ B1 Battle Droid)
--Average speed and health.
-1. Blaster Carbine: High rate of fire, but low damage, ammo count, and poor accuracy.
-2. Light Pistol: Low rate of fire and quick to overheat, but fairly high damage.
-3. Thermal Detonator: Standard grenade, effective against all unit types.
Light Class (Clone Scout Trooper/ B1 Droid Scout)
--High speed and low health. Also has a limited jetpack.
-1. Scout Sniper Rifle: Weak sniper rifle that fires in bursts of three.
-2. Light Pistol: (See Medium Class - Light Pistol)
-3. EMP Grenades: (Republic) High damage and quick to explode, but low radius. Only affects droids.
-3. Concussion Grenades: (CIS) Low damage and small radius, but causes units to be knocked down.
Heavy Class (Clone Assault Trooper/ B2 Super Battle Droid)
--Low speed but decently high health.
-1. Blaster Rifle/ Wrist Blaster: Medium rate of fire and high-power. Better accuracy than Carbine.
-2. EMP Grenades: (Republic) (See Light Class - Emp Grenades)
-2. Concussion Rocket: (CIS) Medium powered rocket with knockback ability.
-3. Thermal Detonators: (Republic) (See Medium Class - Thermal Detonators)
Support Class (Clone Support/ Droid Support)
--Low speed and high health.
-1. Blaster Carbine: (See Medium Class - Blaster Carbine)
-2. Fusion Cutter: Standard mechanic's tool.
-3. Health/Ammo Kits: Droppable health and ammo packages.
-4. Remote Droid: Remote-controlled droid used to spy on enemies and survey the battlefield from a safe distance.
Melee Class (Varies by legion, but includes MagnaGuard and Clone Assassin)
--Stats vary by character.
-1. Melee Weapon: (Again, varies by the character)
-2. Stealth: (Some melee units have stealth ability, but not all)
And then there's the commandos, commanders, and other units, but I won't list those here since their weapons are all so different.
Legions currently included: (List updated 5/25/09)
-Shock troopers
-212th
-607th Legion
-Phase I Troopers
And more eventually, but this is all I have for now. It's a simple proccess to add new legions since I already have the unit templates done, so feel free to suggest legions.
And, per the WIP rules, here are some screens. Note that these are all taken on either Coruscant or Mustafar; these are my favorite maps, and, for the most part, I use them for testing.
Hidden/Spoiler:
Heavy Class of the Shock Troopers on Mustafar
607th Clone Assassin attacking a hapless Battle Droid Scout
Shock troopers strike a pose on Mustafar
The 607th Legion on Coruscant
Random AI Hero action
A Shock Clone Assassin flees from General Grievous
607th Clone Assassin
More AI Hero action
Epic lava burst
Mace Windu
That's all for now. Feel free to post suggestions for maps and characters, but keep 'em realistic. Expect updates on a fairly regular basis. (Although some of my "updates" may simply consist of epic glamour shots
)

Update 5/23/09
Two new force powers: Force Wave and Force Vacuum.
Force Wave
Hidden/Spoiler:
A wave of energy is launched in the forward direction. Everything in it's path is knocked backwards. A direct hit may cause much stronger knockback. Also causes some damage.
Force Vacuum
Hidden/Spoiler:
All units in a specific radius are forcefully drawn towards the user. Similar to the Force Pull attack, though this variation affects units in a full circle around the user. Also causes some damage.
That's it for today. Like always, suggestions are welcome, but nothing wierd/wacky/overpowered/whatever.
------------------------------------------------------
Update 5/28/09
I added in some legion-specific classes. These are classes with specialized roles for the most part, such as demolition or sniping.
Hidden/Spoiler:
ARC Elite - A powerhouse of destruction. Boasts a rifle, rocket launcher, wrist flamethrower, and grenades.
212th Stealth Trooper - Uses a cloaking device to sneak behind enemy lines and cause havoc. His major downfall is lack of armor, so when playing this unit, stealth is key.
Shock Advanced Sniper - The best of the best when it comes to ranged combat. A single shot can kill most standard infantry.
More specialist units for the droids and other clone legions as well, though I'm not done with them yet. As always, comments and suggestions are welcome.

posts.author: Xavious
posts.content_text:
Two new force powers: Force Wave and Force Vacuum.
Force Wave
Hidden/Spoiler:
A wave of energy is launched in the forward direction. Everything in it's path is knocked backwards. A direct hit may cause much stronger knockback. Also causes some damage.
Force Vacuum
Hidden/Spoiler:
All units in a specific radius are forcefully drawn towards the user. Similar to the Force Pull attack, though this variation affects units in a full circle around the user. Also causes some damage.
That's it for today. Like always, suggestions are welcome, but nothing wierd/wacky/overpowered/whatever.

posts.content_text:
I added in some legion-specific classes. These are classes with specialized roles for the most part, such as demolition or sniping.
Hidden/Spoiler:
ARC Elite - A powerhouse of destruction. Boasts a rifle, rocket launcher, wrist flamethrower, and grenades.
212th Stealth Trooper - Uses a cloaking device to sneak behind enemy lines and cause havoc. His major downfall is lack of armor, so when playing this unit, stealth is key.
Shock Advanced Sniper - The best of the best when it comes to ranged combat. A single shot can kill most standard infantry.
More specialist units for the droids and other clone legions as well, though I'm not done with them yet. As always, comments and suggestions are welcome.

posts.author: Xavious
posts.content_text:
Well, it's been a while since I last posted here. I haven't really had anything to show for the past few days. Anyways, I've got good news, and I've got.... more good news.
Firstly, and most importantly, all my ZeroEditor problems I was having with my main computer are fixed! I'm now 100% back on track, and I'll be able to get stuff done much faster.
I've also got a new map today: Geonosis: Arena. Now, I've seen this map done a couple times before, and the thing that always bothered me was how flat and open it was. I know that's how it was portrayed in Episode II, but it doesn't make for very good gameplay. I made sure to give mine plenty of height variation, rocks, hills, whatever. I'm also planning on creating a simple campaign mode to reenact the arena scene from Epsiode II, where you'll play as the Jedi and hold out in the middle of the arena, fighting off battle droids, Jango Fett, battle droids, an acklay, and more battle droids. More info on that soon.
Without further ado, here's some screenies.

Oh, and by the way, this isn't that big Geonosis map I was alluding to earlier.

posts.author: Xavious
posts.content_text:
I have a question for all of you.
So I did some multiplayer testing last night on the random legions and units. What I found was the host would get one legion, and the clients' legions could get a different legion at the spawn screen. However, upon the client spawning, they would in fact be the host's legions.
For example, say I was hosting. Say I got the 607th as the randomly loaded legion. Then someone else joins, and on their spawn screen they have Phase I clones. They pick a character, but then spawn as the 607th equivalent instead.
What I want to know is how big a factor you all think this is. Would you prefer the legions to be preset for multiplayer, or have random legions and the aforementioned problem for everyone who joins a multiplayer game? (Or is there some way to force the client to adopt the same random characters from the spawn screen? I doubt it, but you never know.)
Oh, and on another note, all localizations for all the characters and weapons so far are done (Took me about an hour and a half... I hadn't done any of them earlier). The mod's starting to come together and look more like a finished product. I'm not ready for a release any time soon, just wanted to let you all know that it's coming along.

EDIT: And... here's the promised update/ announcement.
Mod release is just around the corner! I'd say I'm at about 90-95% right now, and I should have a release either this weekend or the weekend after. However, there have been a couple changes and cuts that I made for a couple different reasons.
First off, Venator and Space Coruscant are cut from this version. They simply aren't polished enough. That and Venator looks sloppy with the lack of matching props, and the bridge-to-hallway teleport ends up looking silly and working rather poorly. These maps may be included in a future version or released seperately with UB:TCW era support.
Secondly, I removed the 327th legion and replaced them with the 501st legion. Why? I already had a yellow legion (the 212th) and wanted to add more variety. I also wasn't too fond of the skins I had or the look of the characters in general.
Thirdly, I spent a good chunk of time remaking
all
the clone skins using Icemember's white clones as bases. I did this not only to give a better sense of unity to the skins, but also because I couldn't figure who had made the skins I was using. And it does feel better having more of my own work in the mod, rather than borrowing stuff from others all the time.
So here's a couple (okay, quite a few) new screenshots to drool over.

I've been watching your topic for quite some time and although having not watched whatever show or movie this battle is from I was interested because it looked like it would bring in some new things to bf2, which it did to a degree.
Now onto the part where I say what was good and what was bad.
The good: The new models, they were very high quality and really added a new feel to the map. Campaign, a nice touch to add to the map, not many people ever even learn lua advanced enough to make a campaign.
The bad: Bot pathing, the bots had no clue what they were doing on the big barrier (which would be of no use either way there was no way to get up there besides jumping so perhaps you would consider making it a ramp) even for me I had to jump onto the barrier to use it and then after that there was no cover at all. The texture on the crystal, it looked far too transparent and had little to no detail. The biggest problem with the campaign itself was the inability to win, since the AI immediately head to the artillery (so did I) the final objective walkers were long gone before the objective even began. Also the objective going to the "ambush" was very annoying, I was playing as Obi wan and it took me 10 minutes just to get up there and just to get a bunch of AI who get killed in 3 seconds and jump down myself. The final problem with the map is it's linear, Gameplay is too simple and boring all you need to do is get in the ATTE or artillery and fire away to win.
Overall it's a nice looking map, but it falls victim to the same thing that all first new maps do.

A good way to ensure the droids aren't destroyed too early but still appear in the map is to increase their health or health regen rate with the SetProperty command at the beginning of the map, then when the objective starts, return their health to what it should be. This is used in some shipped campaigns and a lot of the objective modes I set up to make objects indestructible until the exact moment they should be.
Here's the function to use:     SetProperty("objectname", "odf property", value)
In your case, you should probably set it up like this:
Add these lines to the script before your objectives start, or on the start of the first objective:
SetProperty("turret1", "MaxHealth", 999999)
SetProperty("turret1", "CurHealth", 999999)
Then at the start of the objective where the turrets are destroyed, use the same function and just change the health values:
SetProperty("turret1", "MaxHealth", 1000)
SetProperty("turret1", "CurHealth", 1000)
Substituting "turret1" for the names you gave the tri-droids in ZeroEditor and the health values for whatever you want them to be. If you need examples, just look through some of the scripts for the shipped campaigns.

Nono, I do not run an advice column; the modding forum is your best bet. All you can do is learn some basics (there are a couple basic examples in the EYN thread), look at stock campaigns, and read the scripting_system doc. Start small (just onenterregion objectives or something) and work your way up.
No one should ever ask general questions to one specific person, because we have a whole forum for asking those questions to a group of people, more than one of which can give an answer. If you think there is one question that is specific knowledge, you might only ask one person (although it is still usually best to post a thread in the modding forum), and the question (which has since been removed?) was a pretty specific question. ForceMaster wrote:
not change the health.
I.E. I need increase the health of tri-droids bencause the AI destroy it before the objective show.
This is not your problem. You can leave them at the same health level and it will be fine.
You have two problems. The first is that one tri-droid starts outside the shield, so the turrets destroy it right away. Your second problem is that the clone troopers are getting inside the tri-droids somehow, so it's actually the droids destroying them, not your team. posts.author: Post by Frisbeetarian
posts.content_text:
I think that it's a good idea to have them there from the beginning, you just have to fix the couple things I said:
You have two problems. The first is that one tri-droid starts outside the shield, so the turrets destroy it right away. Your second problem is that the clone troopers are getting inside the tri-droids somehow, so it's actually the droids destroying them, not your team.
The first is fixed by just moving the tri-droid back into the shield; a simple ZE fix. The second is fixed by adding the following to the tri-droid ODF under each building section:
Code:
Select all
Pilottype		= "self"
and then setting it to the CIS team in ZE. This will mean that no one can get inside the turret, but that it will remain on the CIS side and function fully.

It's Finally Here!
--KHIMERA BATTLEGROUNDS--
by YaNkFaN
What you actually get with this mappack

Review by Nihillo
My review (directed not only at Yankfan as a report, but as an actual review instead):
Khimera is the best map pack I have played for SWBF II. Now, I know there aren't many of them, but the few we have available are mostly high-quality projects produced by talented individuals -making a mod is not for amateurs, I suppose- and while it is difficult to compete with the likes of Maveritchell and Xavious, Yankfan manages to sucessfully equal said standards and introduce some conceptual innovations.
This "planet-pack" (as I'm going to refer to it) is a collection of a variety of thematic battle fronts, each with a different gameplay:
Beach reminds me of Vietnam War games, patrolling gunships offer air support to a batallion of troopers attempting to break enemy fortified defenses, a suicidal mission that might end up in disaster or in the beggining of an invasion; while the defenders provide a phenomenal resistance, they are not overwhelming and the invaders have many advantages that can be used to spearhead the attack on enemy lines, providing a well balanced gameplay.
Islands (a misnomer, in my opinion) is a forestal map that reminds me of the battle of endor in a way, command posts are always changing hands, but none of them seems to be at a tactical disvantage, with fortified gun emplacements protecting the scattered CPs from flanking and direct attacks; instead of the frontal clash of forces present in Beach, Islands has a chaotic nature.
Most of the combat in Jungle happens at the river crossing the map, walkers and repulsor tanks support a contingent of soldiers in their advance, while smaller groups battle it out in the woods and ruins.
Plains has a cinematic beginning, with walkers striding alongside troops, in CW conquest there is even a dropship bringing a perfectly functional AT-TE to the battle. The map has a simple layout and is very open, with the ocasional structure here and there, while it stands as a great map by itself, it's just too... well... plain when compared to the other maps.
Streets, the shining (actually dark) jewel of the planet pack, is a ruined city (capital?) of Khimera, if you have played Virmund City, you should expect a similar quality in the structure of the city, the gameplay, however, is paced differently, while Virmund has various levels with intersections at the end of linear passages, Streets has one plane divided into two sections by a river and connected by a few bridges at the middle, CPs are placed in interesting areas across each sides. The ambience here is astonishing, literally a picture that comes to life, I won't describe it because I don't want to spoil it for anyone.
The overall theme is sustained throughout the pack, with glimpses of the next map clearly visible at the horizon, a really nice touch that makes the maps feel like they are set near each other.
The classic Yankfan sides are present, which is always a good thing, players should expect some new weapons, though. The Clone Legion is plain white, an interesting (but not completely original, I am aware of that) take on the usually colorful Clones, possibly implying a transitory stage of alleigances, whatever the case may be, I like them, they have a simple and somewhat formal appearance, similar to stormtroopers; Droids have the good and old beige B1s with a OOM security droid and a B2 thrown in the mix; The Imperial faction looks similar to that we have seen in Servorum, grey troopers with insignias of the empire while Rebels have Bothans as snipers and their usual camouflaged uniforms.
Yankfan's Khimera planet pack is a testament to the authors professional skil, a solid mod with a beautiful scenario and -most importantly- excellent gameplay. be sure to download it as soon as it is released, because this is a must-have for everyone.

README
Hidden/Spoiler:
[code]
------KHIMERA BATTLEGROUNDS by YaNkFaN-------
Installation Instructions
Put the folder labeled gamedata in C:\Program Files\LucasArts\Star Wars Battlefront II or wheverer your gamedata folder for the game is located I have set up the directory properly.
Your Computer will ask you if it is ok to overwrite the files click yes to all (this mod does not edit the shipped game what so ever).
Once in BF2 the Khimera maps will not look like other modded maps instead they will be the color of the shipped BF2 maps (this was done on purpose and again did not edit the shipped game at all)
Suggested settings
Lighting- High/Medium
Water- High (if your computer can handle it) many of the maps 4/5 actually have some water in them this really will increase your gaming experience to have water on high
Shadows- off (unless you have a high end computer, I personally see no need for shadows)
Khimera Battlegrounds is a planet pack with 5 maps that all take place on the same planet.  Each map comes with 3 random environments (except plains this has 2).   The 3 random environments are a sunset like environment, a clear day, and a rain or story environment.  Each map also has a total of 6 random heros (3 for each faction) which are different every time you play.  In total the mappack has 12 random heroes which are random each time you play
Also for those who downloaded the Dark Times mod by Maveritchell, all 5 maps have a Dark Times mode.
Khimera Battlegrounds was built in such a way for the maps to be played in order.  Not playing in order will not cause any problems with the gameplay but playing in order will enhance gameplay and provide a more logical, smoother flow to the maps.  The suggested order to play is the way they appear (top to bottem, also alphabetical) in the map picking screen.  The order is Beach, Islands, Jungle, Plains, Streets.
Khimera Battlegrounds as far as I can tell is online compatable.
Khimera Battlegrounds uses a lot of assets created by others, I would just like to take the time to thank them for their work.

posts.author: H_BOMB
posts.content_text:
Okay, cool mappack. Though there is some room for improvement. Here's my review:
Beach-
The map itself is very cool, expeccially when its raining.
Except the gameplay is unbalanced. It is nearly impossible for the side that is assaulting the beach to win. Even if you try to capture as many CPs as you can. I'm not exactly sure why its unbalaced, but it just is.
Islands-
This map is much more easy to win for any side. Though it does require a bit of strategy, but thats not a bad thing.
Like others have said, the ground texture is extremely bright on all lighting settings, shadow or not, and with bloom on the ground glows.
Jungle-
This one is fun, but extremely laggy. Which makes sense, but I don't think it would impact the feel too much if it lost some foliage in some places.
Plains-
My favorite, for the epic battle feel. Nothing wrong that I can see with this one. One suggestion would be too add some of the props used in jungle in the area behind where the sides emerged but, you know its optional.
Streets-
Very eerie, a little bit hard, but its still winnable. My only suggestion would be to add a small canyon or waterfall to where the big river in the middle emerges because as of right now, it has no visible begginning or end. Its just... there.
Still, it was a very fun map pack. I had some suggestions about the sides too, but I'll wait until I try them all out first.

posts.author: Caleb1117
posts.content_text:
Alpha channel is a layer in an image that will make parts of it transparent, when used as an image.
Take this for instance, it is a typical square/rectangular image, the Alpha channel around the person (The Tick) makes the background that was in the original image nonexistant.
Its sort of like erasing things from an image, but it makes stuff invisible instead of just white.
I just noticed I missed a spot in-between his antennae, darn.

posts.author: RepSharpshooter
posts.content_text: Well don't cut the tgas, just stretch/shrink them. They'll come out the same ingame. For those of you who don't understand uv coordinates, it's all relative to the bitmap. Typically it's between 0 to 1 in the U and 0 to 1 in the V.  It doesn't matter how big, what aspect ratio etc. 0,0 will ALWAYS be the bottom left, and 1,1 will ALWAYS be the top right of the texture. If I had a 1324x6849 texture, I could scale it to 256x256 and it would look the same, except for pixelation.

posts.author: VF501
posts.content_text: PsychoHamster, an easier way to do UVs for complex models is to make the model but dont merge the parts.  After its done and UVed and textured, select the pieces then merge them via Create Polymesh>Merge and in the pop up dialog find the area that reads Materials, UVs, Vertex Colors, Weight Maps and hit the merge button there.\nTo break your model back up into its component meshs, select all the polygons or points of the part you want to extract, then go to Create Poly Mesh>Extract Polygons (delete).  This will take the selected polygons/points/edges and make a new mesh out of it.   Just make sure you select all the points of the section you want and no extra ones.

@Fluffy: An easy way to texture is to go into the Texture Editor (Either from a Window Drop down or bring it up via alt+7), then layout the UVs onto a blank tga using Planar, Cylindrical and Spherical Sub-Projections to get the best fit.  Then in the Texture Editor go Edit>Stamp UV Mesh.  In the PPG for that, select the image to be a tga.  What this will do is stamp the UV layout directly onto your original .tga and make a copy of it.  The default save spot for it is on your project folder.

posts.author: FragMe!
posts.content_text:
redgroupclan wrote:
Anyone got advice on doing the treads? Otherwise Im just putting a bunch of cubes together and takin what I can get
Yes, make a cylinder with enough U segments to make the tread look correct in the next part. You only need 1 V and open bottom and top (the little check marks at the bottom of the creation thing. Still in the creation window make the height the width of the tread. Close the creation window. Rotate the clyinder so it is aligned where it should be on the model. Freeze all transforms. now scale the cylinder so it fits correctly. Then if you want the treads to "move" in game there is a tread tutorial that is pretty good.
An alternative on the cylinder (leave the top and bottom closed) is before rotating make a second cylinder that is taller and slightly smaller in diameter. Select the first clyinder, then from the modify menu do a boolean difference selecting the second cylinder. This will give you poies on both the inside and outside of the tread. Freeze modeling on the first cylinder. Then do the rotate and scale parts mentioned about. Once you freeze modeling on the first cylinder you can delete the second one.

posts.content_text:
Simple triangulation tut.
Switch the mode to Default
Go to poly mesh
click triangulate.

posts.author: Post by AceMastermind
posts.content_text:
Fluffy_the_ic wrote:
Simple triangulation tut.
Switch the mode to Default
Go to poly mesh
click triangulate.
No, pre-triangulation doesn't reduce the total number of triangles.
There seems to be a bit of confusion concerning this so i'll try to explain, when you create a cube it's made up of 6 quadrilaterals(or quads) and each quad is made up of 2 triangles(12 total), you just don't see the invisible edge dividing each quad. Modeling in quads is easier than trying to model in triangles but the software(XSI in this case) is always calculating the total triangles even though you don't see any visible triangles. The # of triangles displayed in XSI will be the same number that the game will see.
Hope that helps....

@Darth-Revan: Your stuff is really well done, no matter if its one object or several.  One object is more for polycount optimization (and bragging rights), but for moving parts and/or some models multiple objects are better from a design/development point of view.  It still looks great, but you can reduce the amount of polygons on cylinder endcaps though to make them more efficient.  I hope you find someone good at UVing and Texturin or become proficient at it yourself.  Those models deserve a great texture.
@ YouJediJunkie: I think you're one of the best "from scratch" texture makers around, but I gotta do this one myself (well at least for the first skin) because I need the practice and unless you wanna do all my Halo stuff, because I also want a consistent texture quality/style for this.  However, I'll send 2 UV stamped tgas your way later on to see what you can cook up (most likely once I get off my butt and UV the armor, the Elite itself is UVed).  I do consider it flattering to have you offer.
Oddly enough, I find it easier and faster to layout UVs for a Organic character model rather than a Weapon/Mechanical.  It took me 3-4 hrs over 3-4 days of work to do the layout for a 600 odd Poly SMG, but only 2-3 hrs over 1-2 days for a 2000+ poly elite.  I bet the Armor will take 2-3 days.

posts.author: Post by Frisbeetarian
posts.content_text: He's talking about the extra circle inside the base of each cylinder for the wheels and the extra circle around the center of the lateral surface for the cylinders. This adds 10*2 tris*2 bases/wheel*10 wheels + 10*2 tris*lateral surface/wheel*10 wheels = 600 extra tris on the wheels alone. Your other cylinders have similar problems. The merging polygon method works, but can mess up the model if you do it too much.

posts.author: Post by Maveritchell
posts.content_text:
elfie wrote:
@Obiboba3po - Thanks for the help! Is this fixed now?
(1)
For some reason it keeps sinking through the terrain. Do I need hardpoints on all the wheels for it not to do that?
(2)
Also, if I scale the mesh through a msh.option file to make it smaller, will the nulls be out of place?
(3)
1) You did reduce the polies on the wheels by a lot, which is all I was talking about, and that is better. There are still a couple places you could reduce them more (there's still an extra division on that cylinder in the middle of the gun barrel, for example), but it's basically fine. One thing that'll help you is, usually, whenever you create a cylinder, go ahead and set "U" and "V" divisions to 1 instead of the default 2, and then delete the extra divisions on the cylinder caps. It's a good habit to get into.
But it still doesn't look like it's really UV'd. Of course, I have no idea what you want it to look like, so I could easily be wrong, but the lines on it (the texture) are very odd in how they show up on the model, and, for example, the wheels have the same texture as everything else. I would take a little more time and gain some experience in applying texture/s.
2) It's sinking through the terrain probably because you have the dummyroot at 0,0,0 and the model is sunk below that in XSI. Wherever the dummyroot is (and it
should
always be at 0,0,0) is where the "bottom" of the model is going to be ingame. The collision might move it up if the vehicle spawn is high enough, but if the vehicle spawn is on the ground like it should be, your vehicle will just fall through, I would imagine.
3) No.

posts.content_text:
so i haven't made a map in a year or so, and i finally had an urge to make something new (yankfan convinced me)
I consider it my best map, and this time, I didn't overdo the unit count
I know some of my maps in the past have had too many units..
The map consists of 5 cps, each in a unique type of position. It has a ravine, a tunnel/cave, manor houses, a fort, ruins, and a forest.
In the forest,  there are two manor houses, and on the other side of the map, a fort. In the center there is a big clearing where there are ruins. connecting the fort and manor houses there is a ravine which also has a tunnel connecting it to the clearing.
I have not done sides yet, but there are both Clone Wars and GCW.
Republic vehicles — hover tank, barc speeders
CIS vehicles — AAT,STAP, dwarfspider droid
Empire vehicles — ATST, speeder bike
Alliance vehicles — combat speeder, speeder bike
