- Readme -
----------------------------------------------------------
----------------- Operation:  FM -----------------
-------- Starwars: Battlefront 2 map --------
----------------------------------------------------------
Version 1.0
Author: ****
Screennames: Archer01 or Theodranis
Email:
theodranis@hotmail.com
Date: Jan 25, 2007
----------------------------------------------------------
----------------------------------------------------------
Description: Welcome to the map known as "Operation: Ferret (out the) Master". It is a mini story-based adventure that includes RPG style elements. This map was an experiment to see how far the game's engine could be taken through modding. Some features have been pushed as far as the game will allow, while others might still be able to go further.
!!!!!!----> VERY IMPORTANT: 'Friendly Fire' must be turned 'On', otherwise the dialog engine will not work and the story cannot be progressed.
!!!!!!----> To unlock conquest mode: Since few people seem to actually read the readme before playing and since map exploration is part of the initial impact of the story mode, the map has been setup so that conquest mode must be manually unlocked.
Unlock: Find the "<SWBF2Directory>\addon\OFM\unlock_con.bat" file and run it (double click). The "unlock_con.bat" batch file automatically replaces the "addme.script" file with the "realaddme.file" file. You could replace the addme yourself if you wish, but it is simpler to run "unlock_con.bat". Once unlocked, conquest mode will remain available for selection.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*** Technical Issues ***
If you are having trouble running the map (i.e. crash to desktop), try lowering the Lighting graphics option. There appears to be a bug in the game that causes it to crash on certain computer configurations. The large amount of water present on the map is the suspected cause of these crashes (unconfirmed).
Also make sure that all of the map's files are where they are supposed to be. See the installation section of this readme for the full list.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*** Background Story ***
It has only been a short time since the activation of Order 66 and the newly formed Galactic Empire has begun its expansion across the galaxy. Although the Emperor's plan was flawless, an unpredictable element has allowed a few Jedi Knights to escape their fate; and now with the help of a group of traitors that call themselves the Rebel Alliance, these fugitive Force users have gone into hiding. Although the hunting down and elimination of the fugitive Jedi is among the highest of the Empire's priorities, keeping the entire galaxy under control has been a strain on its vast, but finite resources. As a result, some of the assault forces sent to search for the runaways have been severely underpowered. This is where our story begins...
One of the fugitives has been tracked down to a remote, recently settled planet near the outer rim. The planet has only a few sparse colonies spread widely across its surface, and it is unknown if the Jedi is hiding in one of these settlements, or somewhere else away from the populace. Due to the lack of available resources, only a single StarDestroyer has been dispatched to hunt the Jedi down. The commander of the ship has had experience with Jedi knights in the past and quickly realizes that a single ship is not enough to blockade the entire planet. Unless the exact location of the target is know, any form of open search would be futile and allow the Jedi time to escape. The commander instead instructs his helm officer to come out of hyperspace well out of sensor range of the planet, and he then proceeds to select several of his best troops and issues orders for them to prepare for a mission of espionage.
You are one of the troops selected for the mission. Each of you will be sent to a settlement disguised as a traveling civilian. A stealth-ed imperial transport will shuttle you to a remote location on the planet's surface. Once there you will await the arrival of a salvaged civilian transport that will ferry you to your designated settlement. You will then begin collecting any information you can regarding the hidden location of the Jedi. If you happen to discover the fugitive's hiding place, immediately contact the StarDestroyer and inform command of the location. The battleship will then move into blockade position above the target and dispatch reinforcements to assist in the assault. Bombardment of the location using the StarDestroyer's main weapons is not an option; elimination of the target must be confirmed! Be advised, after you arrive at the settlement the salvaged transport will depart once you leave the platform, as it will be required to land the other personnel at their designated locations. From that point you will continue the mission on your own. Good luck.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*** Gameplay Notes ***
[Story mode]
- This map uses a checkpoint system. When you respawn, certain story related characters and enemies may be replaced based on where they were since the last checkpoint you reached. Certain objectives are also reset depending on checkpoints. Note: Sidequests and character XP are NOT affected by the checkpoint system. Only story related factors are.
- Use the "Talk" weapon (secondary) to open a dialog with an NPC. (Friendly Fire must be ON for it to work correctly)
- There is a basic levelup system in this map. As you eliminate hostiles and complete sidequests you will gain experience points. Gain enough points and your character will levelup and be granted a health bonus. Talk to the "Level Master" in the bar to find out what level your character currently is.
- The Blue number at the top of the screen is the player's number of "retries". The Red number is the remaining XP points needed to reach the next character level.
- To talk to the bartender from across the counter, you have to raise the targeting reticule a little bit above his head. Doing so gives the Talk weapon enough clearance over the counter to hit him.
- Short characters are sometimes a little difficult to target with the talk weapon, just change position a bit and try again.
- The water cave is escapable, but sometimes you have to jump a bit.
- The damage region at the mouth of the cave is there for a balance reason.
- No matter the conditions, the BlackSun sidequests are always available for completion.
[Conquest]
- The Sky Speeder bomb drops from underneath the craft and explodes a short time after landing on the ground (like a grenade). Three are dropped in a salvo.
- To reload/repair the skyspeeders, you'll likely need to land. The repair droids work very slowly (once every six seconds or so).
- There are only three spots on the map where the flyers can land.
- The hidden CP in conquest is selectable for spawn, you just can't see it on the map.
- Heroes are randomized at game start.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
*** Request to the players (You) ***
Please do not discuss anything on the forums that might be considered a "spoiler". That includes stuff relating to the map's layout, specific story-important dialog, etc. On a similar note, posting screenshots is also not desirable, unless they too do not give any hints away. Please do not mention any specific details about the Fugitive Jedi online. Thanks.

posts.author: Post by trainmaster611
posts.content_text:
***TIPS***
1) Get in the LAAT. WHen you get to the landing platform walk along the edge of the water half submerged and you will be protected by the hills. Once you get into the city, you will no longer be attacked.
2)Talk to the Black Sun operative outside the back of the bar. He will tell you to go back to the landing platform and get some cargo and bring it to his customer. Walk back along the edge of the water and talk to the operative standing there. He will give you the cargo. Go back to the city for safety and sneak aout the back. Head torwards the mountain and stay close to the water. Go to the mountain stay along the inner edge of the bay. Once you get to the far side of the peninsula/mountain, there will be three Black Sun people. One of them is the customer. Talk to them and the customer will take his goods.
3) Head back to the city (along the edge of the water) and go back to the Black Sun Operative out back. He willl give you a shield generator.
4)Talk to the Black Sun guy INSIDE the bar. He will ask you to collect some holocrons. I'm not sure why. There's about 7 of them. 6 are accesible. 5 are one the island that you are on. The 6th one is on an island that is possible to walk to (you will sustain minimal damage). The 7th one is on an island you can not get to. I'm still not sure how to get there. Everytime you collect one, it is automatically delivered to the Black Sun guy in the bar so you don't have to bring it back.
To find these holocrons without getting killed, pause the game and use freecam. Once you find one, you can go there and get it.
5) Now just wander around town and talk to a few people. Go back in the bar and talk to the bartender. He will tell you to talk to the jawa. The jawa is behind the city walls out on the beach. The jawa will complain about losing the key to his skiff. He will tell you to talk to some Wild Hunter or soemthing like that. Go back in the bar and talk to the guy in the green shirt. He will tell you that if you help the jawa he will give you some info about the rebels. He will also tell you that an acklay has the key in his lair. You will see an acklay half way to the mountain gaurding some rocks. Sneak up behind the Acklay and look at the rocks. There will be an underwater cave. Run into the cave really fast and you will see some floating white rings. Run into this and you will pick up the card. Go back to town and talk to the jawa. He will thank you.
6)Talk to the green hunter in the bar again and he will tell you that he saw rebels sneaking on and off of a certain island. Go to the jawa and talk to him.  He will lend you the skiff and you will be ferried to the rebel island. There's like four or five rebels there. Hide from them so they don't notice you. Get the holoron and make a run for the computer by the hut.
7)Then run to the skiff and it will bring you back. When you get to the beach, the town is deserted and the jawa and the green hunter will be standing on the beach. They will tell you that the townsfolk turned out to be rebels and when he says that, an ocean of green and black uniforms will pour out of the city walls firing at you.
You are supposed to go back to the landing pad to radio for reinforcements but there is nothing there so there is nothing you can do. On top of that, the rebel army, wookiee savages, thiefs, and nomadic hunters are closing in on you like a swarm of guys around a naked hot babe. I have no idea how to communicate for reinforcements to the Empire so someone else will have to complete this for me.
[/b]

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
Hey guys, it's me again. I've been checking over the last few pages of this thread and here's what I've read and what I'm thinking of doing about them...
1 - Early character healing
I'll setup another Black Sun operative in the town. He will be standing next to a CTF-like marker (the glowing circle). When you enter the circle, your character will be healed back to full health, but it will reduce your XP a bit. You won't lose any levels, but it will just take that much longer to reach your 'next' character level.
2 - Capturing the hill CP
The difficulty of taking that CP is dependant on 'when' you attack (timing the attack waves), but in the interest of possible improvement I put forward another idea: What does everyone say to making it so it takes longer to capture that CP, but the rebels cannot recapture it (ie any reduction in their hold stays the way it is)? On top of that, the rebels will be able to spawn at the CP even after it has been neutralized. So what do the players think; would this be better or worse?
3- Map size/too much walking
This is still only my second map for this game. I'm still getting used to the difference in the sense of scale between the editor and the actual game. Resizing the map now would require completely redoing the entire terrain/regions/paths/etc, so I afraid that's not going to happen. I will however make an effort to avoid this type of thing in any future maps I create. (Third time will hopefully be the charm)
4- No multiplayer support
Teancum guessed right; I set it up so the map would not appear in the multiplayer list. I did that because I had structured the mission scripts for a single player game only. While the script-based engines I created for this map 'should' work in multiplayer (dialog, level, sidequests, etc), the main quest was not setup to support several players moving around the map at once. Some of the scripted events might not execute in correct order thus possibly breaking the quest. Considering the attention this map has gotten, I'll likely end up doing another (time permitting), and I'll attempt to make that one multiplayer compatible. I would say I "will" make it multiplayer compatible, but there are a few things in the game engine that work differently in multiplayer than they do in singleplayer. Experimentation would be required.
5- Acklay not moving
That's an issue with the game's AI. I could make the Acklay more ruthless and chase you all over the map, but that's not what I was aiming for.
6- Moving around under water for a long time
I guess it is possible to move around underwater for a while at higher levels, and while it might be odd, it doesn't really destroy the gameplay does it? I'm assuming you were exaggerating Penguin when you said "10-25 mins". Even at level 10 the health loss is fairly steady. How long can 1490 HP last? The shields shouldn't add on too much either.
7- CTF circle near the landing pad
It is a little "sunken" into the ground. I'll raise it up a bit and make it more noticable.
8- Holocrons
To make thing clear: There are 8 holocrons in total, and none of them have to do with the main quest. They are all just simple "pickups" hidden around the map. Would anyone like a map of their locations? I have one if you're interested.
9- Leaving vehicles
If you enter a vehicle, and then leave after it starts moving, you'll have "missed the boat" so to speak. If that happens, respawning should reset the transport.
So, I think that's it. Did I miss anything?
Also, just to keep everyone updated: With Christmas fast approaching I haven't had the time to work on my modding. Hopefully that will change as the month goes on and I complete most of my holiday tasks. I wish you a "happy gaming" until then, and thank you all for the input.

This map isn't your standard battlefront map, in case you haven't noticed. It's set up like an RPG; there's bound to be walking.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
Hey everybody,
You haven't heard from me in a while, and there is a very simple reason for this (besides daily activities); two words: "Twilight Princess". Now that I've finished it (being rather disappointed in the final boss), I've gone back to trying to get this map wrapped up. I know this map is now "old news", but I would still like to finish it up if I can. Here's how it's going so far:
*Most Noteable changes:
- It is now dangerous (damage region) to dive into deep water (greater than 6-8 meters or so).
- The hill CP can no longer be retaken by the rebels, but it takes much longer to capture it.
- A heal zone is now available in the town. Using it heals you completely, but reduces your XP total a bit.
- Many of the previously missing sounds now work (still missing the transport's sounds, but I may just skip those)
*Things I'm still working on:
- Conquest ( !!! ). Because of the map's layout, the conquest mode is being a pain in the rear to make interesting.
- Updating/Finishing the Readme
- Bug fixes, etc.
*Some things that I could use a little input from you players about:
- Now that there is a heal zone in town, ten (10) retries seems a little too high and I'm thinking of lowering it to around five (5) or six (6). Can anyone see anything wrong with that?
- I know that Zerted's shell can be used to 'cheat' by giving the player infinite reinforcements. I'm just wondering if I should stop people from being able to use that feature?
- SolidFett, what did you do in the Fake Console that caused that reaction?
- Should I bother with the Conquest mode? How important is the mode to everyone?
I'll be coming and going every so often while I poke away trying to finish this thing up. Thanks again everyone for all your input and support! Have fun in the mean time.
- Archer01
Map Hint:
For surviving the conquest part -> Level up early, and make sure you finish the Holocron side-quest right after the battle begins.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
Oops, I’m sorry Ateas… I must have missed your post.
The idea of a mini-mmorpg is also an excellent idea, but it might not be possible. Many of the game’s interface functions work "differently" in multiplayer than they do in single player. Take the dialog system in OFM for example: The dialog text is displayed using the mission objectives message functionality. Unless I’m mistaken (I haven’t tested it yet), that function displays the text for all human players playing. So when anyone uses the Talk weapon, everyone would see it no matter where they are.
I have a few ideas about how one might get around that problem, kind of a “middle-ground” if you will, but I don’t want to say anything until I know it would actually work.
There is also another thing to consider: The stability of the exe itself. I’m fairly sure the game has a variety of memory leaks that the developers never got around to fixing. These leaks aren’t really a problem when a map is only running for an hour or so; once the battle ends, memory is cleared, and a new map is loaded. However, a map left running for a long time would no doubt fill up the memory of the server, and then it would crash after it runs out of space. Out of curiosity (some people do some weird things sometimes), has anyone out there started a map that cannot be won through CP captures, activated infinite reinforcements and then left it running for a whole day if not longer? I’m not suggesting you do that, I’m just asking if anyone has.
Anyway, I’ll look around and try some stuff out when I get the chance, but I’m not very optimistic about it. As I said above, it is an awesome idea, but the game itself may not be up to the task.
Other Force Heal related note:
It restores 1/3 of the max HP of the character. If the Jedi is at 2/3 health, using the ability will bring him up to full health. I think it’s fair since you can’t block while using it, and the ability can only be used three times per spawn (unless you run across a Gonk droid of course). I'm still curious what other people think of it though.

posts.author: Vyse
posts.content_text:
Here is a quick tutorial on how to apply specular lighting to your models. It adds a real time light glare onto your models. This really makes your models look great!
I have not tested the flag on a object, just a player model and weapon.
Before starting the steps what I have found so far is that it appears you can't have the mesh have more than 1 texture on it. The mesh can only pull from 1 texture. However, I'm still testing this so maybe there can be more. Also I havn't removed the sun flare from my .fx file so I don't know if there has to be a flare or not but right now I have a sun in the map and it works.
Instructions:
1)Make sure your global lighting placed in Zero Editor has the "Cast Specular" on yes
2)Using the Battlefront 1 edit flag, select your polygons with the U key, (Basicly just ctrl+A to select all the polys) then open the edit flag dialog box. Scroll down to Render Specular under the Render Types and hit ok. You do not need to call out a texture or anything.
3)Munge the map and your done.
Options:
You can adjust the angle of your placed light in Zero Editor to change when the light hits on the mesh.
The ending effect is below. The pic are from looking in different directions, you can see the lighting has changed.

posts.content_text:
Here's a much improved version of Sarin Cem. There's a few new units (clone medic!), and reskins all around.
The readme:
V1.1a by Rikino
An update to my second released map, Sarin Cem: Constraint.
This takes place at some point in the Clone Wars
Sarin Cem, an outer rim planet, has come under attack by the CIS. The droids have
already taken a power station and the outlying swamps, but the clones have holed up
in their mountain base.
Another version is possible, maybe in a mappack or somthing.
Description:
- The map is a swampy region surrounded by mountains. The CIS start on both sides of the map; over the swamp and inside a power station. The Republic starts inside their fort and in the tunnels.
Features:
- Tunnel system underneath the mountains.
- New units: Clone Medic, Magnaguard Inquisitor, and Jedi Commader
- Custom skins (and a normal battle droid unit) for the CIS. (by Dragon93)
- Custom skins for the Republic.
- Plo Koon as hero for Republic. (yodaminch's) (with assets from -_-)
Issues:
- There is no boundry.
- Some of the CIS AI acts weird; they run around in the back swamp and generally stay away from the fighting.
- Some tree's collision meshes are offset; sometimes you'll be able to run through one and others your shots will stop midair.
- In one tunnel, it's raining inside. That one area is jinxed or somthing, no matter what I do, it keeps raining.
Installation: Copy the folder "GSP" to the directory "Star Wars Battlefront II\GameData\addon".
You need to have the patch installed.
WARNING!!!: I've seen a few other maps with the filename GSP. Sorry for the inconvenience, but both maps will NOT work at once. You will need to delete the other one if you have it. I did not see them until after I had gotten a good deal into this map, and if I had, I would have named it somthing else.
If you have questions or comments, email me at JoeRikino(at)gmail.
Feel free to distribute, just be sure to drop me a line.
Thanks to:

Dragon93 for the awesome CIS skins
yodaminch for the Plo Koon assets
-_- for making the Electric Judgement Force wave, and
salvaging
the bacta syringe model.
The folks at gametoast with all their sage advice.

OF LUCASFILM ENTERTAINMENT COMPANY LTD. ELEMENTS TM & (C) LUCASARTS, A
DIVISION OF LUCASFILM ENTERTAINMENT COMPANY LTD.

posts.author: t551
posts.content_text: Float refers to a floating-decimal data type.  Just type in a number instead of <FLOAT>.\nJust be aware that the game does not display a re-scaled object correctly.  If the original model would not be visible from a certain location, then the new one is not, even if it should be.\nActually, I'm not sure whether this is true all the time.  It may just be when the old model is occluded by another object in te world, or it may occur anytime that the old object is not visible, such as when your starfighter is turning away from it.

posts.author: Post by Nihillo
posts.content_text:
I don't know about Nova, but personally, I think it's a mix of luck (lots of luck), a quick finger and some practice.
Sometimes I pause the game and go to free camera to take a shot, but it's not good enough, then I take a look around and find something very interesting happening; a good example of that would be one pic of Pestox I posted a few pages back, the one with the rebels and the empire fighting, with a stormtrooper coming out of cover and pointing his gun to a distracted rebel, that event was completely random -I wasn't even there! I was far away, at the other side of the map- I thought it was cool and took a picture, that my friend, is pure luck.
When I intend to take a picture, I just pose my trooper and/or shoot stuff, there's no trick to it, the hard part is pausing the game at the right time, it may take several tries to get a good picture.
@Nova Hawk: yeah, awesome pics.

title: Space Assault map with Dragonum's models and more!
author: Ace_Azzameen_5

posts.author: Ace_Azzameen_5
posts.content_text:
Dragon's Lair Nebulum
A space map with Dragonum's Venator and Providence class capital ship models and a large dose of [GT]Ace Azzameen 5.
I set up your basic Clone Wars assault map using the new models. I had to get creative since the models, though in separate pieces, were not designed to be used for assault. Oh well, I slapped the extra destroyables on and got creative with the bridges, used a bunch of LUA work-arounds, and now assault is playable.
[GAMEPLAY NOTES]
To destroy the republic's bridge, you have to blast their weak points, the main window! Vent the atmosphere and let those meatbags freeze and suffocate.
The Providence's bridge is divided into two structurally isolated halves, but destroying one half should take out the other!
Features
-Dragonum's models, yay!
-An auto-turret like mainframe to take out or reactivate indoor roof turrets.
Problems
-Some of the fighter spawns are a little too high
-The Providence has a glitchy hangar floor, must use other models to work around.-FIXED, Mr. Floor has been Dealt with.
-AI Gunships like to ignore the land command node on their spline. . .so, take back the cockpit if one drives you too close to the CIS hangar floor.
-lod distance maybe needs some work
-ship objective icons are mis-oriented
-targets missing destroyed geometry
Todo List
Complex Interiors- The interiors are simple and slapped together and use the crummy defualt layout, I plan to change this
-Better turrets, bottom turrets
-Maybe a new side with faster fighters but probably not
-Frigates.
-More flyer splines. Yay splines.
-More fighters in the air.
-Balance . ..
-portals and sectors
-destroyed  geometry-make a blown up looking texture for everything and use it. Maybe I'll stick some "rubble" objects in.
-Tatooine-FIXED-now a blue purple awe-inspiring nebula, either the dragon is one of them Mystical Dragons, or I'm painting it orange red and yellow.
This list may now be inaccurate, since I switched to Dragonum's new versions with proper collisions.
Download Link
Just in case no one noticed his name everywhere,
Cred's to Dragonum for the ships, which are the backbone of the map.
The Invisible hand models wer originally made by, as referenced in Dragonum's readme, Bertie.
I still deserve lots of credit for putting setting up assault, making the interiors,
and
the security console. And the splines,  .. .so many splines.  . .

posts.content_text:
My review:
First off:
Best space map ever. Just saying so.
Gameplay:
Awesome. There needs to be a little work on the splines for the flyers, but that's understandable.
Balance:
You said you need to work on it, but I think it is great as is, almost. The Republic has to dogfight to get those points and the CIS has to use brute force. I say give the Republic more fighters (no bombers) and keep the ARC-170s as they are, but give the Venator more shields so that the CIS has to work to score hits.  If you add a V-Wing, add it as a fighter or interceptor. No bombers for the Republic.
Bugs:
All the collision bugs have been mentioned, and I got one random crash, but I think that was my CPU.
Recommendations:
-More Units (Seems you have done that)
-Hanger transport (Seem to be working on it already)
-More detailed interiors (Seem to be working on it as well)
Great job overall. A "flawed masterpiece" if I may quote EraofDesann from one of his reviews.
-Alpha

posts.content_text:
Setting up moving treads for Star Wars: Battlefront II
1. Make a 2 wheeled model (bicycle etc). Make sure the wheel treads are separate objects.
2. Select the polygons you want the tread textures on.
3. Apply the tread texture to both wheels.
4. Select the front wheel tread object and name it wheel_front
5. Select the back wheel tread object and name it wheel_back
6. Export
7. Make a hover vehicle ODF and add this under [Properties] (refer to cis_tread_hailfire.odf)
Code:
Select all
WHEELSECTION		= 1
WheelTexture 		= "wheel_front"
WheelVelocToU		= 0.4
WheelOmegaToU		= -1.1

WHEELSECTION		= 2
WheelTexture		= "wheel_back"
WheelVelocToU		= 0.4
WheelOmegaToU		= 1.1
If your model only has one wheel or tread object then you only need one WHEELSECTION.
WheelTexture refers to the polygon mesh objects with the tread texture applied, not the actual texture.
8. Next create a msh.option file and put these switches in it:
Code:
Select all
-keep wheel_front wheel_back -keepmaterial wheel_front wheel_back
Original tutorial
Hidden/Spoiler:
Ok, I'll just try to make a short tutorial right now.
Setting up moving treads for Star Wars: Battlefront II
step 1. Make your Model.
step 2. Select the polygons you want the wheel textures on.
step 3. Apply the wheel texture on the wheels.
step 4. Select the right wheel polygons (or the left, whichever you prefer to start with)
step 5. File -> Pandemic Tools -> Edit Flags
step 6. Set Render type to 3 (scroll, you can look them up
HERE
) (Thanks squipple
)
step 7. At  PolygonID, fill in
wheel_right
(if you selected the left wheel, call it
wheel_left
)
step 8. Do the same for the other wheel, keeping in mind that you call that one differently.
step 9. Export as normal.
step 10. Make a hover vehicle (hover height = 0) odf and add this:
[code]WHEELSECTION		= 1
WheelTexture 		= "wheel_right"
WheelVelocToU		= 0.4
WheelOmegaToU		= -1.1
WHEELSECTION		= 2
WheelTexture		= "wheel_left"
WheelVelocToU		= 0.4
WheelOmegaToU		= 1.1[/code]
WheelTexture refers to the Polygons, not to the actual texture.
Next create a msh.option file and put these switches in it:
-keep wheel_left wheel_right -keepmaterial wheel_left wheel_right
It should work right now.. although I've got the feeling I forgot something.. Oh well, try it out

posts.author: Post by AceMastermind
posts.content_text:
This is an example of a single wheeled test vehicle that I made:
In XSI, I have a tread object on my vehicle named:
wheel_whatever
I selected the polygons on that tread object and went to:
File
>
Pandemic Tools
>
Edit Flags
then selected:
Render Type 13
(Render Rotate)
closed the ppg then exported.
In the vehicle ODF where:
Code:
Select all
WHEELSECTION        = 1
WheelTexture   = "wheel_whatever"
WheelVelocToV       = -0.8333333 //V = vertical texture scrolling, U = horizontal
WheelOmegaToV       = 0
wheel_whatever
is the name of the tread object in my hierarchy,
and in my msh.option file I type:
Code:
Select all
-keep wheel_whatever -keepmaterial wheel_whatever
and that's it, munged the side, played and had working treads.
Your tread object should have a separate texture applied to it in XSI.

posts.author: Elmo
posts.content_text:
For those of you who don't know how to implement this into your map, Ill write a small tut. :p
1. there should be 4 folders- msh, odf, effects, and sound. (you need the rep side for this to work)
2. open up The rep side folder, and put the files that are in the msh folder (UT AT source files) in the msh folder of the rep folder. (there are 2 folders in the source files msh folder) - (skins for GCW and skins for CW) Do what i said above, for all the folders, copying the files into each corresponding folder. (there is no sound folder in the reps sides folder, So just copy the whole sound folder.)
3. In the rep req file where all the other folders are, put this line under all the others, "rep_hover_utat") make sure you work out all the quotes and brackets.
4.then- In your req
folder
copy a vehicle req file, and delete everything in there and then put this in it-
ucft
{
REQN
{
"class"
"rep_hover_utat"
}
}
after that, you should be all set (assuming you know how to place the vehicle spawn in the ZE and all
)
Edit: also, when you munge make sure to select "rep" in the dropdown bar under sides...

posts.author: Saturn_V
posts.content_text: It wasn't any fancy "Hollywood magic" type movie editing, I used the language tool to edit the kill message to say "pwned".  Best mod I ever did, lol.  Easiest way is to do it on a map by map basis.  Have a look on Psych0fred's board for the list of localisation keys.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text: Hey Saturn,\nHow do you get into these localization strings?  I'm trying to remove the word "the" from the captured CP message for example, "The Empire has captured THE command post").  Can ya give me an idea how to do it?\nRip

posts.author: Post

posts.author: Saturn_V
posts.content_text:
1. Download the localisation string list from Psych0fred's board.
2. Open it in a word processor and search for what you want (eg, search for captured)
3. Use the Localize button in BFBuilder to launch the Localize tool to add the scopes and keys for whatever you want to change.
Right click to get a menu to add a scope or a key.  The key is the last part of the string, which you type a name for in the box in the middle (ie, not the comments box).
So for the CP "The", a quick search for captured shows:
game.infomsg.captured	"%s captured The %s"
game
is a Scope.
infomsg
is a scope.
captured
is a key.
"%s captured The %s"
is the string displayed, so change it to
%s captured %s
Then change the corresponding key for losing a CP (
game.infomsg.lost
)

Let try putting it this way:\nWhat do I do with the localization strings that I can read from Fred's site?  I can certainly read them and edit them, but how do I get the changes into the game?  That's my question.  Yes, I know it involves the localization tool, lol.  But I can't find any menu for editing the word "the" out of the capture text as Saturn explained in that earlier post.  That's what I'm trying to do.  Rends' tutorial doesn't say anything about it.\nRip

posts.author: SteveK14
posts.content_text: set up the scopes and keys and put the words you want in the right pane, and SAVE. Click on the disk icon or go to the file menu and save. That's about it.

posts.author: Saturn_V
posts.content_text:
the localisation string,
game.infomsg.captured "%s captured The %s"
breaks down as
scope.scope.key "<string>"
%s is a placeholder for information fed to the string by the game engine depending on what's happened.
So you right click in the left hand pane, add a root level scope and name it game.  Right click on that, create another scope, call it infomsg, then rc on that and create a key, name it captured.  The key level of the tree is where you type your required text into the text box in the middle.   Select the key and enter the text you want to see in the game in to the middle text box (the comments box changes to match the middel box, it seems), in this case
%s captured %s
This removes "The" from the CP capture message, so if you have a CP called The Barracks (like in the default setup), you'll see the game is now saying
<team> captured Barracks
, so you can rename the CP to The Barracks to correct it.
Now you'll want to add the complementary message string for losing the CP, searching the string list you'll see
game.infomsg.lost "%s lost The %s"
You already have the scope game, and you already have the scope infomsg, so create a new key under infomsg and call it lost.  In the text box enter
%s lost %s
Here's a pic of the tree setup for a bunch of the death messages:

posts.author: Penguin
posts.content_text:
to get maps working online with alot of units or effects, you need to add memory pools for everything.
run your map without playing with max reinforcments and units and then in the log find all the lines saying that a memory pool had to be raised and in your lua add/or raise that memory pool x2
eg:
log
Code:
Select all
Message Severity: 2
.\Memory\RedMemoryPool.cpp(170)
Memory pool "SoldierAnimation" is full; raise count to at least 1376
in your lua put
Code:
Select all
SetMemoryPoolSize("SoldierAnimation", 2752)
[/b]

TRUST ME
.  If you learn things in the right order it all comes naturally.

Not to toot my own horn, but nobody ever looks in the XBOX/PS2/PSP modding forum, and I just want to make sure that all PSP owners are made aware of a mod that will make the PSP version of Star Wars Battlefront 2 worth playing, and actually make it pretty addictive in the case of my friends and I.
http://www.gametoast.com/index.php?name ... pic&t=8808
Trying to capture a CP in the Yavin 4 campaign. Not going so well.
It's a good thing the popup text works! Otherwise, I wouldn't be able to get interrupted in the middle of a battle! These also work on Multiplayer. The message will display and you'll have to press X, but the game won't pause.
Fighting on Coruscant.
More Coruscant, from an alternate perspective.
I'm an Ewok in standard Endor Conquest. I'm about to eat a grenade.
Geonosis. There's the beautiful AT-TE!
The AT-TE clearly works, as the one-and-a-half hailfire tanks will tell you.
Be very very quiet. I'm hunting killer bugs with death rays! In the distance, you can see a spider droid marching and Count Dooku blocking absolutely nothing, like he always does. That's a jet trooper at the top, not another Geonosian.
Playing as a Geonosian on Geonosis Conquest.
Hailfire tanks work just fine. I'm'a go blow up the AT-TE.
LAATs in Geonosis Team Deathmatch.
An LAAT shooting at a spider droid.
Fighting rebel scum in Jabba's Palace. Jabba's beauty shot got messed up by the radar.
The Rancor's about to chew on some Boba Fett.
Local Assault. The Tusken class selection screen.
Local Assault. That Jedi is not my friend. I will crush him.
Local Assault. The Jawa class selection screen.
Local Assault. That Tusken is not my friend. I will cut him.
Anyone who's played Hoth on the PSP knows that battles never get anywhere near this messy.

A Jawa on Mos Eisley Conquest.
A Tusken on Mos Eisley Conquest.
Defending Naboo from the Trade Federation!
The Droid Marine on Naboo. I just thought this was a good time to show that there are more than ten AI per team in the battle because nineteen AI are selecting one class.

More Utapau.
Playing as a Wookie on Kashyyyk. Not very interesting for the very last picture.

I had to remove all links/downloads due to the fact that we've been asked to (it's breaking EULA since only the PC has addon abilities).  However, to honor Broadus' hard work I have not deleted this topic.  Please do not ask for these files.  It's breaking the EULA contract.
This file download contains game files from Star Wars Battlefront for the PSP. You cannot hexedit the game files and redistribute them legally. People may do it through email, that's their business, but posting it publicly is not legal. When you do, you are essentially re-distributing parts of the game which is a violation of the software license agreement.
If you have done this, you should remove them, but it's your risk. On the other hand, the forum admins may take issue with it, so you should check with them.
The only files that can be distributed legally are game addons created with the mod tools for the pc within the guidelines of the PC mod tools.
Any hacking or modification you do you cannot re-distribute. The original file was compiled as part of the shipped game. What's legal is lvls compiled by modders using the mod tools.
Giving people instructions is fine, but telling people how to bootleg the game with an ISO is not legal.
Sorry all.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
ok you do this in zero editor it's really simple.
1) Make a big hill using terrain raise
2) use the "terrain height pick" tab and use it to select the terrain height of somewhere 2/3 to the top of the mountain.
3) using the "paint terrain" tab paint the top of the hill flat using the height you selected
4) Using textures make the volcano look real
5) make a small depression on the top of the volcano and add lava textures to it
6) add desired effects timed effects and .fxs.

posts.author: Post by Gogie
posts.content_text:
for the rest of you that still dont understand the misc documentation here is a quick tutorial. ( I have recieved pm's from 3 people askin for it)
okay this is how you use gloss mapping.
1.) Take the texture you are using for the polygons that need glosmapping and save them as a new file with _gloss at the end. (for example MCV_floor_tile1 becomes MCV_floor_tile1_gloss).
2.) Take that copied texture and open it, then using your texture editing program, transform your texture into a grey scale or a monocrhome image. make sure you still save this texture as a .tga. (this is the same type of texture used in bump mapping)
3.) Create a .tga.option file sharing the EXACT same name as your _gloss.tga file. (for example if I had MCV_floor_tile1_gloss.tga, the .tga.option would be MCV_floor_tile1_gloss.tga.option)
4.) Inside the .tga.option place the following lines.
-bumpmap -format bump_alpha -bumpscale 6.0
5.) Load XSI 5.0 or 5.11, and upload your scene.
6.) Using the polygon select tool, select the faces of your polygon you wish to apply gloss mapping to. then open the pandemic edit flags script.
7.) once open select render type 28. do not put anything for data0 or data1, all of your specular details (lower gloss effects) are applied through alpha channels (transparency's) and your phong material (specular decay). in the first texture box put your texture and .tga.option files name down under one name (which is why you want to always have these as the same name). for example, if my textures name was MCV_floor_tile1_gloss.tga, and my option files name was MCV_floor_tile1_gloss.tga.option, then file name I would put down in the box would be MCV_floor_tile1_gloss.... YOU SHOULD NEVER HAVE TO ADD .TGA or .TGA.OPTION IN THESE TEXTURE BOXES. make sure you have the full folder name as well behiund your texture. so it should look like this in the texture box.
C:\BF2_ModTools\data_mcv\worlds\mcv\msh\MCV_floor_tile1_gloss
8.) simply export and your set.
(note: if you desire there to be just glossing effects without the bump mapping you simply set the bump scale from 6.0 to 0.0 inside the .tga.option file.)
here is a pic of my glossing in starforge.

posts.author: Post by [RDH]Zerted
posts.content_text:
Looks good.
Some things to consider:
Was this test done in MP?  Units tend to fall through moving objects much more in MP than in SP.  The demo elevators I made worked great in SP, but were almost worthless in MP (teleporters or rotating elevators worked better).  Your elevator looks like it might be moving too fast for MP.
Are you going to let the AI use it?
What happens to units when they fall under the elevator?
What happens to units when the elevator falls under the tem?
Its hard to tell, do you have inner and outer doors or is there just an empty space on the floor the elevator isn't in?
I would recommend putting a floor and death region under the elevator.  That way, it will catch all the mines/detpacks/other objects that fall through so the server won't have to process them falling forever.

posts.author: Post by [RDH]Zerted
posts.content_text: I did a few intresting things with the elevator I made (yours is much better/safer being inclosed and a 'real XSI model').  A sniper could drop an auto-turret in a certain way to make it stay in place while the elevator moved through it.  Standing on top/below the turret would make you fall ontop/below the elevator as it moved past and the turret blocked your movement.\nPutting the turret in the center of the elevator and throwing a mine on it was a good way to blow up helpless units while they are traveling in the elevator.  A player looks into the open elevator, see no threats and goes in.  The doors close and the elevator starts moving.  Suddenly a turret appears out of the floor (or ceiling) and BOOM, the player is dead.  I can't think of a way to block this kind of attack.\nOne more thing to consider:  If a player is standing in the door when they start to close, does the unit die or end up insde the wall?

A good tip is to create 1 massive pallet with all your map textures on , so that the engine is only looking for 1 (2 + the lowrez) throughout your map. Basically lots of textures slows the map down more than a few extra polies.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
A mesh can have polygons with n vertices. So called N-Gons. Gon from old greek for vertex, I seem to remember. N for Number.
Since no engine and no renderer can render N-Gons (quads included) everything gets triangulated before it can be displayed. If you put a "non-trianglulated" model into an engine, it'll either triangulate on it's own, or just crash.
A quad with 4 vertices for example has a polycount of 1. Evidently. The engine does not care for this polycount, as it is only interested in the tri-count, which would be 2.
The more polygons or N-gons (which is pretty much the same, since poly means something like many), the more tris. Thats pretty self explanatory. So if you waste polys, you waste tris automatically.

posts.author: Post
posts.content_text:
@Caleb': To easily add faces to the inside, do the following:
1) Select the edges around the top of the cylinder shape.
2) Press ctrl+D to duplicate the edges.
3) use the scale tool to scale them in slightly along the X and Z axis.
4) Press Ctrl+D again to duplicate once more.
5) Drag these new edges down on the Y axis, until it reaches the bottom of the canister.
If all goes well and i didn't miss out any steps, you should have some nice faces inside the canister
EDIT: an easy way to select edges such as the ones on the top of the cylinder is to use the loop selection. To do this, you must be in the raycast edge selection mode. Then Left click on one edge. then middle click on another edge to loop select all the edges at the top of the cylinder

posts.author: Post by AceMastermind
posts.content_text: You can also press alt+MMB to select a single edge loop or you can select multiple edge loops by holding shift+alt+MMB.

posts.author: t551
posts.content_text:
But triangle count is the TRUE polygon count, because all polygons are actually drawn as triangles.
That's why flat polygons with lots of points have weird shading problems- Softimage is triangulating them before they are rendered.
Right now it's 1197 polygons.
If you're worried about the Art Doc guidelines, you shouldn't be- those numbers are only a rough approximation anyway.  However, for things like player models, it actually refers to the number of triangles-because you almost always triangulate enveloped models in order to have better control over how they deform.
InyriForge is a girl. Not a guy.

now I know an import when I see one.
the handle is no doubt an import
supporting evidence:
1.) triangulation going two different ways at the same exact same coordinace...
2.) I assume that you are new to XSI since you have never seemed to post a model on this site... this "talent" seems to come out of no where.
3.) if this was imported from another program, all poly's would have subdivisions, but I do not see sub divisions on the blade, only on the handle, which leads me to beleive that the blade was either deleted or imported, show me a picture of your XSI explorer. the handle however is imported. whether it be from another game, or simply from another program, but those are not the way XSI makes subdivisions on its own objects. all subdivisions should face the same direction on a cubic surface unless it is imported.
ill post more screens for demonstration or my words in a sec.
[edit]: never mind I see the subdivisions on the blade now.
here I made a replica of his hangles rectangle
as you can see, when we subdivide, all the subdivisions except the center edge face the same direction.
and when we show a wireframe, it shows us even more, insterad of being perfect triangles, the turn into X's, why? because even the poly's on the other side face the same direction, so when we move those triangles 180 degrees to face the back, they face the opposite direction, so if this wasnt an import, instead of triangles in the wireframe, it would have X's
sorry for the jr.moderating.

posts.content_text: Ace Mastermind is correct. Starship Troopers is the answer, or to be more specific, the Arachnid Warriors from Starship Troopers.  They are the "grunts" of the bug forces and pwn some serious arse.   Aklay Animations might be possible, but the skeleton (ie. the neck/head area) would seriously mess up the front end.  IF you are really determined to use this ingame.  Study how the sekeletons are setup and try to build a new one.  Custom Animations will be a pain though, esp the walk cycles and the attacks.\nVery nice model, but sharpen the interior section of the claws, which will also reduce the poly count as hard edges use less polys then cylinders. Also, the legs are connected to another section mounted below the body (similar to a tank turret mounted n the tank body), so a new poly mesh is needed.  For the middle section of the body, you could probably flatten tthe ends out (the parts that are inside the rear and head) and use less polys that way.  Still, all in all, very nice model.

posts.content_text: Press the "I" key to go into raycast edge select mode and select and delete edges or edge loops(alt+MMB) that do not affect the topology of the model, redraw new edges( \ key) or pre-triangulate parts if necessary, to keep roundness.

Well, a dummyroot is a null which is parent to the rest.. I think you won't need it though. Create a null at the part you want the fire come from, and call it hp_fire
